point_description: Sarah's forever routine: microcurrent, vitamin C, azelaic acid, daily SPF, a split double cleanse, LED, tretinoin recovery nights, and a bedtime slugging ritual.

am.title: Cleanse
am.product: Balea MED Ultra Sensitive Wash Gel
am.description:
I like to use a gentle cleanser in the morning, even though you technically don't need to cleanse in the am unless you feel very greasy or sweaty, it is fine to skip cleanser to keep the barrier calm.

When you do cleanse, keep it gentle and non-stripping. Since I am close to the German border I can easily get to a dm, I love their brand Balea for affordable skin and haircare. This Balea MED wash gel is boring in the best way, sensitive-skin friendly, and not trying to do too much.

am.title: Rose Water Spray
am.product: Mario Badescu Facial Spray with Aloe, Herbs and Rosewater
am.description: Mist after cleansing or as the first step if skipping cleanser. Damp skin makes the next watery layers spread more evenly, and the ritual part matters too: it makes the routine feel less like homework.

am.title: Microcurrent
am.description:
Use NuFACE for about five minutes with NuFACE Hydrating Aqua Gel Activator or another conductive gel. The gel matters because microcurrent needs slip and conductivity; do not try to drag the device over dry skin.

I like this step in the morning because the instant lifted look is wasted on a pillow. If I'm in a hurry, this is one of the steps I skip.

Read my full rave review on this product here.

am.title: Vitamin C
am.description:
This is a Polish brand that I'm trying out for the first time with this Vitamin C serum. Of course there are plenty of alternatives on the market, at various price ranges and stabilities. I will have to do a whole blog post on Vitamin C serums to explain, but in a nutshell, don't go for the cheapest option and make sure you keep it in a cool dark place. I keep this one in the fridge.

Vitamin C is the brightening and an antioxidant step in the morning routine.

am.title: Azelaic Acid
am.description:
Azelaic acid is one of those quiet workhorse ingredients. I use this one from France at 15%, but there are easier to get alternatives in the US at lower concentrations like The INKEY List SuperSolutions 10% Azelaic Serum Redness Relief Solution. In Poland they have a 20% OTC that I want to try once I'm finished with my tube of Azéane.

Use as the pigment, redness, and texture-support step after vitamin C if your skin is tolerating the combination. If skin feels reactive, use this less often or separate it from other actives. Consistency matters more than forcing it every single morning.

Read my full review on this product here.

am.title: Moisturizer
am.description:
Use only if skin needs it, especially in winter or when the routine feels a little too active. This is not mandatory every morning; it is the comfort layer when your skin is asking for one.

Keep it light so SPF can still sit properly on top.

Read why this cult cream won me over here.

am.title: Face Oil & Gua Sha
am.description:
Use a face oil for slip, then gua sha with gentle upward and outward strokes. There are many gua sha shapes, but I like this kind of square shape best vs the triangle. I've linked the tarte Maracuja oil but really I have a proprietary blend that I'll have to write a post about soon.

This step belongs before SPF. Oil after sunscreen can disturb the protective film, so finish any massage before moving on to the final sunscreen layer.

am.title: SPF Eye Cream
am.product: Supergoop Bright-Eyed 100% Mineral Eye Cream SPF 40
am.description:
Tap around the eye area before face SPF. Many sunscreens sting around the eyes, but this one does not so this keeps the eye area protected without making the whole morning miserable.

Read my full glowing review on this product here.

am.title: SPF
am.product: La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVMune 400 Anti-Dark Spots Fluid SPF50+
am.description:
SPF is always last. Do not layer oil, moisturizer, or gua sha on top of this because it can interfere with the sunscreen film. If you can only do one thing in the morning, it is sunscreen. This is the non-negotiable step for dark spots, sun damage, and keeping the rest of the routine worth doing.

I am currently looking to replace my beloved Josie Maran SPF that was discontinued. Sadly, this one is not a good replacement.

Read my full critical review on this product here.

am.title: Lip Balm
am.description:
I have always had a love/hate relationship with lip balm, my lips seemed addicted to it and yet still irritated. Then I discovered beef tallow balm, Hudsalva is great because it avoids the beeswax and petrolatum feel that can make lips angry instead of comfortable. I read an interview with Alicia Vikander who swears by it so I had to try it. It is sold at a pharmacy in Sweden and at Boots in the UK according to her.

I used to be able to find it on Amazon, but once that became unreliable I found this US-based option by Vintage Tradition.

pm.title: Cleansing Oil
pm.product: SKIN1004 Madagascar Centella Light Cleansing Oil
pm.description:
This is the first cleanse, and it is mostly here for makeup, water-resistant sunscreen, or those nights when I know I reapplied SPF like a responsible adult. Massage it onto dry skin for at least a minute so it can break down sunscreen, mascara, and whatever city/day residue is sitting on your face, then add water to emulsify before rinsing.

I do not use this because I want my face to feel squeaky-clean. I use it so the second cleanser does not have to do all the heavy lifting. If I did not wear makeup and barely left the house, I can skip this and go straight to Tatcha.

Read my full honest review on this product here.

pm.title: Double Cleanse
pm.description:
This is the second cleanse after the oil cleanser. It gets rid of any leftover oil, sunscreen film, and general residue so my skin is actually clean before LED or tretinoin. I only use a small amount and I do not scrub, because a cleanser should clean your face, not start a fight with your barrier.

The Deep Cleanse lives up to its name and makes my skin feel clean without that tight, over-washed feeling. If I did not wear makeup or reapply much sunscreen, this can be the only cleanse.

Read why this cleanser won me over in my review here.

pm.title: LED Mask
pm.product: Solawave Wrinkle Retreat Pro LED Face Mask
pm.description:
Use on clean, dry skin before leave-on skincare. LED fits best here because it gets a bare-skin window and does not have to fight through oil, slugging layers, or sunscreen.

This linked mask is a U.S. brand, Solawave's current Wrinkle Retreat Pro LED Face Mask, but I use a European LED mask by Koanna. Any LED mask with at least 630–660 nm red and 810–850 nm near-infrared works.

pm.title: Treatment
pm.description:
I use prescription tretinoin 0.05% on treatment nights and let it sink in for a few minutes before continuing. This is a good time to do something else, like brush your teeth, so the step has a little breathing room.

Because tretinoin is prescription-only, the link goes to Differin Gel as a popular over-the-counter retinoid option. French A313 is another well-known retinoid-style option. On recovery nights, skip retinoids and use The Ordinary Multi-Peptide + Copper Peptides 1% Serum instead.

pm.title: Rose Water Spray
pm.product: Mario Badescu Facial Spray with Aloe, Herbs and Rosewater
pm.description: Mist after the treatment has had a few minutes to settle. This brings back a little dampness before hydrating serum, which helps the next step spread without tugging.

pm.title: Hydrating Serum
pm.description:
Apply a hydrating serum while skin is slightly damp from the rose water. This is the cushion step that makes the retinoid routine feel less austere.

The Ordinary hyaluronic acid works here, or you can swap in Celimax Noni Ampoule when you want a more soothing, plush serum.

pm.title: Eye Cream
pm.product: Beauty of Joseon Revive Eye Serum : Ginseng + Retinal
pm.description:
I have so many favorite eye creams for evening but this is what I am currently using. As long as it has a retinoid I am willing to try it. This one is very nice and refreshing, perfect for summer since it isn't heavy. Of course, one of my favs my Glow Recipe was discontinued (the Avocado Melt Reintol Eye Cream). I've also tried the budget option by Inkey List but it is kind of lumpy and not smooth or premium feeling at all.

Read my full critical review on this product here.

pm.title: Moisturizer
pm.description:
Use as the main moisturizer before oil. Embryolisse gives the routine a soft, reliable buffer, especially after tretinoin or on nights when skin needs the extra comfort.

Read why this cult cream won me over here.

pm.title: Face Oil & Gua Sha
pm.product: The Ordinary 100% Organic Cold-Pressed Rose Hip Seed Oil
pm.description:
Use homemade night oil for slip, then gua sha with gentle upward and outward strokes. The linked Ordinary rosehip oil is the straightforward store-bought comparison.

This is the massage and sealant step before the bedtime slugging layers. Give it a little time if you can.

pm.title: More Hyaluronic Acid
pm.description: Use as part one of the bedtime slugging routine. By this point, some time has usually passed after face oil, so Ialuset acts like the plush humectant layer before the final occlusive seal.

pm.title: Slugging Balm
pm.description: Use as the final face layer to seal in all the moisture. This is the true occlusive finish of the bedtime slugging routine: everything hydrating goes underneath, Egyptian Magic locks it down.

pm.title: Lip Mask
pm.description:
Finish with the Laneige lip mask. It stays cushiony overnight, which is exactly what you want from the final lip step before bed. My lips are never dry in the morning.

Read my full rave review on this product here.

sources.headline: Hailey Bieber Revealed Her Full Nightly Skin-Care Routine
sources.summary: A 2021 nighttime recap covering her cleansers, peptide serum, barrier cream, oils, eye cream, and Aquaphor lip step.

am.title: Rinse
am.description: In her streamlined morning routine, Hailey starts with the basics: a splash of water to rinse away the remnants of her nighttime skin care. This keeps the morning cleanse gentle, which makes sense for the dry, sensitive skin she has described.

am.title: Mist
am.description:
Use this as the first hydrating step after rinsing. Hailey said that when she is really busy in the morning, she can literally spray her face with this and walk out the door.

Rhode describes it as a hydrating face spray that can be used after cleansing, after moisturizer, or whenever skin needs a refresh.

am.title: Essence
am.description:
Press a generous amount onto the face, neck, and décolleté. Hailey calls Glazing Milk one of her staple products and says she uses it in the morning, at night, and as skin prep.

Rhode recommends applying it after morning or evening cleansing, before Peptide Glazing Fluid and moisturizer.

am.title: Peptide Serum
am.description:
Apply 2-3 pumps to the face, neck, and décolleté. Hailey's 2022 Vogue routine centered on hydration because she has dry, sensitive skin, and this peptide serum was part of that routine.

Rhode recommends following this step with Barrier Restore Cream or Barrier Butter for best results.

am.title: Moisturizer
am.description:
Apply as the barrier-supporting moisturizer step. Rhode recommends using about a half finger-length amount on the face, neck, and décolleté.

This fits the Hailey routine logic: keep skin hydrated, comfortable, and supported before SPF.

am.title: SPF
am.description: Use generously as the final morning skin-care step. Hailey says sunscreen is non-negotiable, and Vogue noted that she likes milky SPF formulas and fell in love with ISDIN Fusion Water Magic SPF on a trip to Paris.

am.title: Lip Treatment
am.description: Glaze lips during the day and reapply whenever they need hydration. In her Vogue routine, Hailey said she does not leave the house without a lip product, morning or night.

pm.title: Oil Cleanse
pm.product: MARA Chia + Moringa Algae Enzyme Cleansing Oil
pm.description: Massage onto dry skin to break down SPF and makeup, then rinse. In her nighttime routine, Hailey said oil cleansing was a newer addition that made a big difference, and she prefers it over makeup wipes.

pm.title: Hydrating Cleanse
pm.product: HoliFrog Tashmoo Water Lily Milky Wash
pm.description: Follow the oil cleanse with a gentle, hydrating cleanser. Hailey said she does not love a super-foaming cleanser and prefers a richer option that does not leave dry, sensitive skin feeling stripped.

pm.title: Essence
pm.description: Press into clean skin before serum. Hailey says she uses Glazing Milk at night too, and Vogue noted that she likes it even when using stronger nighttime products because it helps buffer irritation and support hydration.

pm.title: Peptide Serum
pm.description:
Apply 2-3 pumps and press it in gently. Hailey's newer Rhode-era routines center this peptide serum as a hydrating, barrier-supporting step.

In her earlier 2021 nighttime routine, she also mentioned using Biba Los Angeles Plant Stem Cell Peptide Serum and emphasized that she is a big fan of peptides.

pm.title: Rich Moisturizer
pm.description:
Use a richer moisturizer layer at night. Hailey's famous rule is that if she is not getting into bed looking like a glazed donut, then she is not doing the right thing.

In her earlier 2021 nighttime routine, she also mentioned using Biba Los Angeles Cream Barrier.

pm.title: Face Oil
pm.product: Furtuna Skin Due Alberi Biphase Moisturizing Oil
pm.description: Use only if skin is very dry. Hailey layered a thin amount of face oil for extra glow and hydration, but she also noted that she avoids heavier oils when she is actively breaking out.

pm.title: Pimple Patches
pm.description: Use on active pimples only. Hailey said she likes sleeping in these when she is breaking out because they help a pimple heal faster, and she also likes that they look cute.

pm.title: Eye Cream
pm.product: Ilia Bright Start Activated Eye Cream
pm.description:
Tap gently around the eye area as one of the last skin-care steps. Hailey included eye cream in her nighttime routine after treating and moisturizing her face.

Her original routine used BareMinerals Ageless Phyto-Retinol Eye Cream, but that exact eye cream is no longer available. Ilia Bright Start Activated Eye Cream is a similar available retinol-alternative eye cream.

pm.title: Lip Occlusive
pm.description:
Finish with Aquaphor on the lips. Hailey said she legitimately cannot go to bed without lip balm because she hates chapped, dry lips, and Aquaphor is her go-to.

She also uses a little extra Aquaphor on flaky dry patches when needed.

point_description: A low-fuss routine that puts the money where it matters: daily sunscreen, a beginner retinol, vitamin C, and enough barrier support to keep going.

am.title: Cleanse
am.description: The first step is having a clean palette for the rest of the routine. A nice, boring, gentle cleanser will prepare your skin for what comes next. If your skin is dry and clean in the morning, it is also completely fine to just rinse with water.

am.title: Vitamin C
am.product: CeraVe Skin Renewing Vitamin C Serum
am.description: Apply a thin layer to dry skin before moisturizer. This gives you a straightforward 10% vitamin C step with ceramides and panthenol, for brightening and antioxidant support.

am.title: Azelaic Acid
am.description:
Apply a thin layer after vitamin C and before moisturizer. Azelaic acid is the calm, useful supporting active here: nice for redness, uneven tone, and little texture issues without making the routine feel like a full exfoliation project.

If layering vitamin C and azelaic acid feels spicy, alternate mornings until your skin gets the memo.

am.title: Moisturize
am.description: Use one to two pumps after vitamin C. It has ceramides, squalane, and hyaluronic acid, and it plays nicely with actives. This is not the glamorous step, it is the compliance step: comfortable skin is much more likely to stick with sunscreen and retinol.

am.title: Eye-Area SPF
am.product: Cetaphil Sheer Mineral Sunscreen Stick SPF 50
am.description:
Glide the stick onto a clean fingertip, then tap a generous, even layer around the orbital bone and upper eye contour before face sunscreen. This fragrance-free drugstore mineral SPF 50 is specifically intended for fragile areas around the eyes, though it is an eye-area sunscreen rather than a treatment eye cream.

Keep it out of the eyes and off the lash line, reapply when outdoors, and add sunglasses. A mineral stick can leave some cast; do not solve that by applying less.

am.title: SPF
am.product: Neutrogena Invisible Daily Defense Face Serum SPF 60+
am.description:
Apply generously as the final morning step to face, ears, neck, chest, and hands. This is the most important anti-aging product in the routine because prevention beats trying to undo UV damage later.

If you'd like a drugstore mineral option, try CeraVe Hydrating Mineral Sunscreen SPF 50, though untinted mineral formulas can leave a cast. For a tinted mineral option, Neutrogena Purescreen+ Mineral UV Tint SPF 30 is more wearable and comes in multiple shades.

pm.title: Cleansing Balm
pm.product: e.l.f. Holy Hydration! Makeup Melting Cleansing Balm
pm.description: Use this first on dry skin when you wore makeup, water-resistant sunscreen, or just a lot of SPF. Massage it in until sunscreen and makeup feel loosened, then emulsify with a little water and rinse. This is the step that makes the gentle cleanser actually stand a chance without scrubbing your face like you are mad at it.

pm.title: Double Cleanse
pm.description: Follow the balm with a gentle water-based cleanser. This removes any leftover film and gives you clean skin before retinol without chasing that squeaky-clean feeling.

pm.title: Retinol
pm.description:
Start two nights a week, using a thin layer over the face while avoiding eyelids, lip edges, and the creases beside the nose. This is a gentle drugstore retinol with ceramides and niacinamide, so it fits the point of this routine: effective enough to matter, boring enough that your skin may actually tolerate it.

If you are sensitive, sandwich it between two thin layers of moisturizer. Once tolerated every other night, a dermatologist-prescribed tretinoin is the evidence-maximizing upgrade.

pm.title: Eye Cream
pm.description:
Smooth a rice-grain amount around each eye after the face treatment and before moisturizer. Ceramides, hyaluronic acid, and niacinamide add fragrance-free hydration without stacking another retinoid beside a face-retinol routine.

Keep it out of the eyes themselves. If your regular moisturizer is comfortable here, this remains the targeted step rather than proof that the eye area requires a completely separate universe.

pm.title: Moisturize
pm.description: Finish with moisturizer. If your skin feels tight or flaky, use more moisturizer rather than adding more actives. The goal is steady use over months, not heroic peeling in week one.

point_description: A mid-tier routine for someone who wants the same evidence-based bones with nicer textures: barrier care, vitamin C, SPF, and retinal.

am.title: Cleanse
am.description: Use as a soft morning cleanse, or skip cleanser and rinse with water if skin feels dry. This is the mid-range upgrade because the texture is more cushioning and less utilitarian than a basic drugstore cleanser.

am.title: Vitamin C
am.description: Apply a few drops to dry skin in the morning. This is a 15% vitamin C serum, so it is a bit more ambitious than the drugstore tier. If it stings, use it every other morning or pause until the retinal routine is comfortable.

am.title: Azelaic Acid
am.description:
Apply a thin layer after vitamin C, or mix it into moisturizer if your skin prefers fewer separate layers. This is a good mid-tier brightening and redness-support step, especially if pigmentation and texture are part of the anti-aging concern.

Because this formula also includes salicylic acid, start a few mornings a week if your skin gets dry or easily annoyed.

am.title: Barrier Cream
am.description:
Apply a thin layer over vitamin C. This is where the routine buys a nicer daily experience: richer barrier support, a cushier finish, and enough comfort to make actives less annoying.

For oily skin, swap to Skinfix Skin Barrier Restoring Gel Cream or use a lighter layer.

am.title: SPF Eye Cream
am.product: Supergoop Bright-Eyed 100% Mineral Eye Cream SPF 40
am.description:
Tap an even layer around the eye contour before face sunscreen. This is a mineral SPF 40 eye cream with a peach tint, giving the delicate area dedicated protection without asking a slippery primer sunscreen to migrate right up to the lash line.

If the tint is not a match, the untinted, fragrance-free Ultrasun Eye Protection SPF 30 is the stronger European alternative.

Read my full glowing review on this product here.

am.title: SPF
am.description:
Use as the final morning step. This has that clear, primer-like finish people either love or hate (I'm honestly not the biggest fan).

If you prefer a mineral option, Supergoop Mineral Mattescreen SPF 40 has a subtle neutral tint to reduce cast, but the shade still needs to work for your skin tone.

pm.title: Cleansing Balm
pm.product: Farmacy Green Clean Makeup Removing Cleansing Balm
pm.description:
Use this as the first cleanse when you wore makeup, water-resistant SPF, or just need a more satisfying sunscreen removal step. Massage it onto dry skin, add water so it turns milky, then rinse before going in with your regular cleanser.

If your skin is very reactive, choose the fragrance-free version.

pm.title: Cleanse
pm.description: Use this as the second cleanse after balm, or as your only cleanser if you did not wear makeup and your sunscreen was easy to remove. Keep it practical: the goal is clean skin, not a stripped face.

pm.title: Retinal
pm.description:
Start two nights a week, then slowly build toward every other night if skin stays calm. Crystal Retinal 3 is positioned for newer vitamin A users and gives this tier a more elegant retinal step than the drugstore version.

Do not chase results by layering exfoliating acids on top. Slow and boring wins with retinoids.

pm.title: Peptide Eye Cream
pm.product: Biossance Squalane + Marine Algae Eye Cream
pm.description:
Press a rice-grain amount around each eye after retinal and before face cream. Squalane, panthenol, hyaluronic acid, algae antioxidants, and a peptide provide cushioning without adding a second retinoid to the same evening.

Use less if rich eye creams encourage milia. More product does not make peptides work faster; it mostly makes concealer travel.

pm.title: Barrier Cream
pm.description:
Finish with moisturizer, or sandwich the retinal between two thin layers if you are irritation-prone. A richer cream is not magic, but it can be the difference between quitting retinal and actually using it long enough to see results.

If your skin is oily or the cream feels heavy, use Skinfix Skin Barrier Restoring Gel Cream instead.

point_description: A prestige version of the same routine: iS Clinical cleanser, the OG vitamin C, a luxurious cream, and tinted mineral SPF.

am.title: Cleanse
am.description:
Use a small amount and rinse well. This is a cult luxury cleanser with mild resurfacing energy, so treat it as the polished red-carpet version of a basic cleanse, not the reason the routine works.

If skin is sensitive or you are irritated from AlphaRet, swap this for Augustinus Bader The Cream Cleansing Gel, which feels more like a gentle luxury morning cleanse than a resurfacing cleanse.

am.title: Vitamin C
am.description: Apply four to five drops to dry skin in the morning. This is the luxury benchmark: 15% L-ascorbic acid with vitamin E and ferulic acid. It is expensive, iconic, and genuinely elegant, though less expensive vitamin C products still live in the same useful category.

am.title: Azelaic Acid
am.description:
Apply one to two pumps after vitamin C. This is the luxury azelaic-acid step: more elegant, more expensive, and a little more treatment-moisturizer than straightforward serum.

If your skin is dry, still follow with The Rich Cream. If your skin is oily, this may be enough moisture before SPF.

am.title: Rich Cream
am.description: Apply a thin layer over vitamin C. This is the indulgent comfort step: deeply emollient, luxury-coded, and best for normal-to-dry skin. If you are combination or oily, Augustinus Bader The Cream is the lighter alternative.

am.title: SPF Eye Cream
am.product: Colorescience Total Eye 3-in-1 Renewal Therapy SPF 35
am.description:
Apply around the eye contour before face SPF. This all-mineral SPF 35 eye treatment adds hydration and visible color correction, which makes sense in a luxury routine but also makes shade matching part of the purchase.

For an untinted option, use Ultrasun Eye Protection SPF 30. Neither product replaces UV-blocking sunglasses on a bright day.

am.title: Tinted Mineral SPF
am.description:
Use generously as the final morning step. The tint and iron oxides can add visible-light protection, which is especially useful for melasma and persistent hyperpigmentation, but the shade will not work for everyone.

Untinted alternatives: SkinCeuticals Clear Daily Soothing UV Defense SPF 50 has a sheer hydrating finish, and Skinbetter Sunbetter Sheer SPF 70 is an untinted mineral option, though it may leave a cast.

pm.title: Cleansing Balm
pm.description:
Use this as the first cleanse when you wore makeup, layered SPF, or anything water-resistant. Massage it onto dry skin, add water so it emulsifies, then rinse before your second cleanser.

This is the gentle luxury version of a cleansing balm: fragrance-free, cushiony, and made for sensitive or sensitized skin. Exactly the vibe you want before an AlphaRet night.

pm.title: Cleanse
pm.description: Use this as the second cleanse after balm, or as your only cleanse if you did not wear makeup and your sunscreen was easy to remove. Do not scrub, especially on AlphaRet nights.

pm.title: Retinoid
pm.description:
Start two nights a week and build slowly. AlphaRet combines a cosmetic retinoid with an AHA, so it is doing two active jobs at once. That can be beautiful for lines, pigment, and texture, but sensitive skin should move carefully.

Because this already contains exfoliating acid, do not add a separate peel during the adjustment period.

pm.title: Firming Eye Cream
pm.description:
Press a rice-grain amount along the under-eye curve, crow's-feet, and brow bone after treatment and before cream. Peptides, Proxylane, caffeine, and optical brighteners target the look of crepiness, puffiness, and dark circles without adding another retinoid beside AlphaRet.

The formula is fragrance-free, but avoid applying it directly to the movable eyelid unless the current label advises otherwise.

pm.title: Rich Cream
pm.description:
Finish with a thin layer, or use it before and after AlphaRet if skin needs buffering. This is a gorgeous experience step, but the unsexy truth remains: the results engine is still sunscreen plus retinoid consistency.

If The Rich Cream feels too heavy, swap to Augustinus Bader The Cream, the lighter version in the same product family.

point_description: A KORA-heavy ritual built around double cleansing, vitamin C for pregnancy-linked pigmentation, turmeric glow products, face oil, eye oil, facial massage, and an overnight mask.

sources.label: KORA 2024
sources.headline: Miranda's Nighttime Routine
sources.summary: Miranda lays out quick and luxe nighttime routines with cleansing balm, foaming cleanser, retinol-alternative serum, moisturizer, eye care, face oil, facial massage, and sleeping mask.

sources.label: Marie Claire 2024
sources.headline: Take Notes: Miranda Kerr Reveals Her Ultimate Pregnancy Routine
sources.summary: Kerr discusses her current pregnancy routine, naming Noni Glow Body Oil, Noni Bright Vitamin C Serum, Milky Mushroom Cleansing Oil, Turmeric Glow Foaming Cleanser, Minty Mist, and plant stem-cell retinol alternative products.

sources.label: Vogue 2019
sources.headline: Miranda Kerr Reveals Her Guide to Glowing Pregnancy Beauty
sources.summary: In her Beauty Secrets routine, Kerr applies vitamin C, moisturizer mixed with face oil, Noni Radiant Eye Oil, and uses a rose quartz gua sha tool.

sources.label: W Magazine 2018
sources.headline: Miranda Kerr Gets Candid About Pregnancy, Crystals, and Aging
sources.summary: Kerr describes AM and PM routines with cleanser, mist, vitamin C, moisturizer, face oil, eye oil, and sleeping mask.

am.title: Cleanse
am.product: KORA Organics Milky Mushroom Gentle Cleansing Oil
am.description:
Use as the morning cleanse, shaking first so the oil turns into its milky texture. KORA says this became Miranda's go-to cleanser for both morning and night because it removes makeup and leaves skin soft rather than tight.

Older sources mention KORA foaming or cream cleansers, but the Milky Mushroom Cleansing Oil is the more recent cleanser she specifically talks about as a current favorite.

am.title: Exfoliating Mask
am.product: KORA Organics Turmeric Brightening & Exfoliating Scrub + Mask
am.description:
Use in the shower a few times a week, not as a daily obligation. Marie Claire says Miranda calls this her desert-island product, and British Vogue says she keeps the turmeric mask in the shower and uses it as an invigorating scrub.

This is a polish-and-glow step, so skip it when skin feels reactive or freshly exfoliated.

am.title: Mist
am.product: KORA Organics Active Algae Minty Mist
am.description:
Spritz after cleansing and before serum. Marie Claire says she preps with KORA's Minty Mist, and W describes her using a mist like a toner and refreshing spray throughout the day.

Keep this as the damp-skin step so the serum and moisturizer glide instead of dragging.

am.title: Vitamin C
am.product: KORA Organics Kakadu Plum Vitamin C Serum
am.description:
Apply one to two pumps after mist and bring it down the neck and decolletage. In Vogue, Miranda says her vitamin C helped throughout pregnancy, and Marie Claire says she has used KORA vitamin C through multiple pregnancies because pigmentation can show up then.

The current KORA version is Kakadu Plum Vitamin C Serum; older sources call it Noni Bright Vitamin C Serum.

am.title: Moisturizer
am.description:
Warm a small amount in the palms and apply after serum. In Marie Claire, Miranda says she uses the newer moisturizer morning and night; in W and Vogue, she talks about mixing moisturizer with a few drops of face oil for a hydrated base.

This is the richer glow step, so oily skin may want less than the camera-ready amount.

am.title: Face Oil
am.product: KORA Organics Noni Glow Face Oil
am.description:
Mix a few drops into moisturizer or press it over the top. Miranda repeatedly names Noni Glow Face Oil as a core product, and Marie Claire says she has always used it on her face.

In Vogue, she uses face oil with moisturizer before facial massage, which gives the tool enough slip.

am.title: Eye Oil
am.product: KORA Organics Noni Radiant Eye Oil
am.description:
Roll around the eye area and anywhere small lines need extra slip. In Vogue, Miranda applies Noni Radiant Eye Oil and says she even uses it on little line-prone areas.

This is skincare plus ritual: lightweight oil, rollerball, and a little de-puffing moment.

am.title: Gua Sha
am.product: KORA Organics Rose Quartz Heart Facial Sculptor
am.description:
Use after moisturizer and oil, with upward strokes. In Vogue, Miranda says she likes to keep her rose quartz tool in the fridge and uses it to massage in face oil and moisturizer, support lymphatic drainage, de-puff, sculpt, and work on neck tension points.

Use light pressure. The glow is the goal, not red scrape marks.

pm.title: Cleansing Oil
pm.product: KORA Organics Milky Mushroom Gentle Cleansing Oil
pm.description:
Use as the first cleanse at night, especially for makeup and sunscreen. Marie Claire says Miranda double cleanses even without makeup, starting with KORA Milky Mushroom Cleansing Oil.

Massage on dry skin, add water so it turns milky, then rinse before the foaming cleanser.

pm.title: Double Cleanse
pm.product: KORA Organics Turmeric Glow Foaming Cleanser
pm.description:
Follow the cleansing oil with this foaming cleanser. Marie Claire names Turmeric Glow Foaming Cleanser as the second step in her double cleanse, and KORA describes it as a deep clean that should not dry skin out.

Keep the pressure gentle; the double cleanse should remove the day, not strip the barrier.

pm.title: Treatment Serum
pm.product: KORA Organics Plant Stem Cell Retinol Alternative Serum
pm.description:
Apply after cleansing before moisturizer. Marie Claire says Miranda had been using the plant stem-cell retinol alternative serum, and KORA's nighttime routine places it after cleansing in both the quick and luxe versions.

This is the firming/plumping treatment step in her current routine family, while older W coverage mentioned a nighttime AHA serum instead.

pm.title: Moisturizer
pm.description:
Use after the treatment serum. Marie Claire says Miranda uses the newer moisturizer morning and night; KORA's current nighttime routine also puts moisturizer after the retinol-alternative serum.

If skin is dry, this is where the routine starts to get plush before the oil and mask steps.

pm.title: Eye Cream
pm.product: KORA Organics Kakadu Plum Vitamin C Eye Cream
pm.description:
Tap around the orbital bone after moisturizer. KORA's luxe nighttime routine names Berry Bright Vitamin C Eye Cream here, so that is the direct source-backed product Miranda used in the routine.

KORA now lists Berry Bright as an archive-sale product that will be discontinued soon, so this links Kakadu Plum Vitamin C Eye Cream as the refreshed replacement. Older sources also mention Noni Radiant Eye Oil if you prefer her original rollerball version.

pm.title: Face Oil
pm.product: KORA Organics Noni Glow Face Oil
pm.description:
Press a few drops over moisturizer. W says Miranda uses the same moisturizer and face-oil combination at night, and KORA's luxe nighttime routine keeps Noni Glow Face Oil before facial massage and sleeping mask.

This is the soft seal before the final overnight layer.

pm.title: Facial Massage
pm.product: KORA Organics Rose Quartz Heart Facial Sculptor
pm.description:
Use over the oil when you have time for the luxe version. KORA's nighttime routine includes the rose quartz facial sculptor for facial massage, and Vogue shows Miranda using a rose quartz tool with upward strokes.

This is optional on rushed nights, but it is very Miranda: crystal, lymphatic drainage, and a little ceremony.

pm.title: Sleeping Mask
pm.product: KORA Organics Noni Glow Sleeping Mask
pm.description:
Use as the last step before bed. W says Miranda keeps the sleeping mask next to her bed and uses it to lock in moisturizer; KORA's quick and luxe nighttime routines both finish with Noni Glow Sleeping Mask.

Let it set for a few minutes so it forms that transparent overnight layer instead of smearing straight onto the pillow.

point_description: A glow-focused Ashley Graham routine built around simple cleansing, vitamin C, rich hydration, misting, tools for puffiness and rosacea, diligent SPF, and a very thorough nighttime cleanse.

sources.label: Bustle 2023
sources.headline: The All-Natural Treatment Ashley Graham Gets Again & Again
sources.summary: Ashley talks through her cleanser memories, blackheads, Shani Darden moisturizer, self-tan drops, DermoPH C5 serum, gua sha, and acupuncture.

sources.label: British Vogue 2023
sources.headline: Ashley Graham On Postpartum Hair Loss, Booty Bands And Being Real On Social Media
sources.summary: Ashley describes keeping her evening routine simple with self-tan, vitamin C, a heavy eye cream, and a thick Dermophisiologique moisturizer.

sources.label: Glamour 2021
sources.headline: Ashley Graham Drops Her Skin-Care Routine
sources.summary: Ashley shares a pared-back pregnancy-era routine with cleanser, rosacea cream, toner, Weleda, Revlon rose mist, red-light therapy, jade rolling, and Dermophisiologique SPF.

sources.label: Marie Claire 2021
sources.headline: Ashley Graham Is Serious About Self-Care
sources.summary: Her morning maintenance includes washing her face, St. Tropez Purity Vitamins face serum, SkinCeuticals or Weleda moisturizer, and Dermophisiologique sunscreen.

sources.label: Into The Gloss 2019
sources.headline: Ashley Graham, Model
sources.summary: Ashley gives a detailed Top Shelf routine with Bioderma, SkinMedica, La Suite pads, C E Ferulic, DefenAge, Retrouve, Weleda, Dermophisiologique SPF, and 111Skin masks.

sources.label: Allure 2019
sources.headline: Ashley Graham's Nightly Skin-Care Routine Costs $1,631
sources.summary: Allure recaps Ashley's Harper's Bazaar nighttime routine, including her double cleanse, toner pads, DefenAge serum, Aquaphor, Retrouve eye cream and moisturizer, and Mario Badescu spot treatment.

am.title: Cleanse
am.description:
Wash once in the morning. In Glamour, Ashley says she loves this jelly cleanser because it feels nonabrasive and she only needs one cleanse with it.

Into The Gloss previously had her using SkinMedica Facial Cleanser morning and night, and Bustle notes that she still thinks Cetaphil is a good, clean-and-simple cleanser.

am.title: Toner
am.product: Kristina Holey + Marie Veronique Balancing Hypotonic
am.description: Spritz or swipe after cleansing when skin feels bumpy or reactive. Glamour says Ashley puts a sprayer on this toner and likes it for rosacea, especially when her skin is drier and more dehydrated.

am.title: Vitamin C Serum
am.product: St. Tropez Self Tan Purity Vitamins Bronzing Water Face Serum
am.description:
Apply a small amount after cleansing or toner. Marie Claire says Ashley does a little St. Tropez Purity Vitamins face serum in the morning because it has vitamins C and D.

She has also repeatedly mentioned vitamin C: Vogue and Into The Gloss name SkinCeuticals C E Ferulic, while Bustle says she uses Dermophisiologique C5 Serum before self-tan drops at night.

am.title: Moisturize
am.description:
Apply a light layer before mist and SPF. Bustle says Ashley was trying Shani Darden's oil-free peptide moisturizer because a previous moisturizer felt too thick for summer.

For richer days, Marie Claire and Glamour mention Weleda Skin Food, and Marie Claire says she uses SkinCeuticals Daily Moisture when she wants a different level of moisture.

am.title: Rose Mist
am.description: Mist after moisturizer, before makeup, after makeup, or on the plane. In Glamour, Ashley says Revlon's rose glow mist is her favorite and that she used it before it was even officially out because she thought it was so good.

am.title: De-Puff
am.description: Keep it chilled and roll under the eyes and along the jawline. Glamour says Ashley keeps her Revlon jade roller in the freezer for mornings when she has not slept, and Vogue shows her rolling for puffiness and lymphatic massage.

am.title: SPF
am.description:
Use as the last morning skincare step. Ashley tells Glamour she is a sunscreen guru and likes Dermophisiologique for her face because a little goes a long way and it rubs in nicely.

Into The Gloss calls Dermophisiologique Skin Photo Block her absolute favorite sunscreen because it keeps skin illuminated and does not go on white, and Marie Claire says it is good for her face and sheer.

pm.title: Micellar Water
pm.description: Use on cotton pads as the makeup-removal step when she has a full face on. Into The Gloss and Allure both describe Ashley starting her nighttime double cleanse with Bioderma.

pm.title: Double Cleanse
pm.description:
Lather after micellar water and rinse well. Into The Gloss says her dermatologist recommended this cleanser and Ashley calls it a nice jelly cleanser that is not too abrasive.

Allure also highlights her rule for night: no matter what kind of evening it was, at least wash your face.

pm.title: Tone
pm.product: La Suite Skin Tone Enhancement Therapy Pads
pm.description:
Wipe over clean skin after cleansing. Into The Gloss says Ashley uses these brightening pads from Union Square Dermatology because she has freckles and does not want them to start connecting.

Allure notes they were developed by her dermatologist to help fight hyperpigmentation.

pm.title: Vitamin C
pm.description:
Apply before moisturizer or before the self-tan drops on tanning nights. Bustle says Ashley uses Dermophisiologique C5 Serum before bed on nights she does St. Tropez face drops.

Into The Gloss also names SkinCeuticals C E Ferulic in her nighttime routine, and British Vogue says she loves using vitamin C at night.

pm.title: Serum
pm.description: Smooth over the face after vitamin C or toner. Into The Gloss says Ashley uses DefenAge 8-in-1 BioSerum to help minimize the look of freckles, and Allure places it after her toner pads.

pm.title: Eye Cream
pm.description:
Tap a small amount around the eye area. Into The Gloss says Ashley found Retrouve through Tracee Ellis Ross's routine orbit and likes the eye cream preventatively because she can feel a difference.

British Vogue later says she uses a heavy eye cream at night, sometimes with a bit of retinol, but did not name the exact product there.

pm.title: Moisturize
pm.description:
Use a little; the cream is rich. Into The Gloss says Ashley likes this Retrouve moisturizer because it is rich but still light enough that she does not break out.

British Vogue later says she slathers on a thick Dermophisiologique moisturizer at night, but that source names the brand rather than the exact cream.

pm.title: Self-Tan Drops
pm.product: St. Tropez Luxe Tan Tonic Glow Drops
pm.description:
Use only on self-tan nights, after a shower and after pre-lotioning dry areas. Bustle says Ashley applies two to four drops depending on the look she wants, once or twice a week if she has events or is at home.

British Vogue also says she likes to self-tan every five to seven days at night so she can sleep in it.

pm.title: Spot Treat
pm.description: Dot only on blemishes as needed. Allure says Ashley targets specific areas with Mario Badescu Drying Lotion, keeping it as a spot step rather than an all-over treatment.

pm.title: Lip Balm
pm.description: Use on lips as the final comfort step. Allure calls Aquaphor her tried-and-true lip product, Into The Gloss says it is another go-to for her, and British Vogue says Aquaphor is one of her drugstore skincare favorites.

pm.title: Red Light
pm.product: Dr. Dennis Gross DRx SpectraLite FaceWare Pro
pm.description: Use some nights while lying down or watching TV. Glamour says Ashley swears by Dr. Dennis Gross red-light therapy for rosacea and keeps it next to her bed.

point_description: A fragrance-free drugstore routine built around oat, ceramides, and mineral SPF with no exfoliating acids or retinoids.

am.title: Cleanse
am.description:
Use a small amount with lukewarm water and rinse without scrubbing. This is soap-free, fragrance-free, essential-oil-free, and boring in exactly the way sensitive skin usually appreciates.

If your face feels comfortable and clean in the morning, skip cleanser and just rinse. There is no prize for washing a calm barrier twice.

am.title: Oat Serum
am.product: Aveeno Calm + Restore Triple Oat Serum
am.description:
Press two or three pumps over clean skin before moisturizer. The oat flour, extract, and oil are here for dryness, tightness, and visible reactivity rather than aggressive correction.

This is fragrance-free and tested for sensitive skin, but oat is still an ingredient someone can be allergic to. Patch test first and skip it if you know oats are a problem for you.

am.title: Barrier Moisturizer
am.description:
Apply while skin is still slightly damp. Ceramides, squalane, glycerin, and hyaluronic acid do the unglamorous barrier work without fragrance, essential oils, or a pile of botanical extracts.

Use a little more on dry areas and a little less through an oily T-zone. Sensitive skin does not need every square inch treated identically.

am.title: Eye-Area SPF
am.product: Cetaphil Sheer Mineral Sunscreen Stick SPF 50
am.description:
Glide the stick onto a clean fingertip, then tap a generous, even layer around the orbital bone and upper eye contour before face SPF. It is fragrance-free, mineral, made for sensitive skin, and specifically intended for fragile areas around the eyes.

This is an eye-area sunscreen rather than a treatment eye cream; the CeraVe eye cream at night handles hydration. Keep it out of the eyes and off the lash line, and stop if reactive lids sting or the eyes water.

am.title: Mineral SPF
am.product: Blue Lizard Sensitive Face Mineral Sunscreen SPF 50+
am.description:
Apply generously as the last morning step and reapply when outdoors. This is a fragrance-free mineral option, which can be a better starting point when chemical sunscreen filters sting.

The tradeoff is a possible white cast. Do not use less product to make the cast disappear; switch formulas if you cannot wear the full amount comfortably.

pm.title: Cleanse
pm.description: Massage gently over damp skin and rinse with lukewarm water. If you wore makeup or stubborn water-resistant SPF, remove that first with a fragrance-free micellar water or balm, then let this be the very gentle second cleanse.

pm.title: Oat Serum
pm.product: Aveeno Calm + Restore Triple Oat Serum
pm.description: Repeat the oat serum when skin feels dry or reactive. This is the only treatment layer in the routine, and that restraint is deliberate: calm skin usually responds better to one soothing product than five supposedly soothing products.

pm.title: Barrier Eye Cream
pm.description:
Dot a rice-grain amount around each eye and smooth gently before face moisturizer. It is fragrance-free, ophthalmologist-tested, and built around ceramides, hyaluronic acid, and niacinamide rather than an exfoliating or retinoid active.

Patch test even gentle formulas. During an eyelid flare, stop experimenting and follow your clinician's plan rather than layering more products over inflamed skin.

pm.title: Barrier Moisturizer
pm.description: Finish with a comfortable layer. On very dry nights, press a tiny amount of plain petrolatum over flaky spots after moisturizer. If skin is burning or actively flaring, strip the routine back to cleanser, moisturizer, and SPF until it settles.

point_description: A Sephora-level barrier routine with hypochlorous acid for redness and blemishes, a lipid-rich cream, and gentle mineral SPF.

am.title: Cleanse
am.description: Use a small amount with lukewarm water, or skip the morning cleanse when skin feels dry. This fragrance- and essential-oil-free cleanser gives you a softer, more cushioned wash without trying to exfoliate your face at the sink.

am.title: Redness + Blemish Mist
am.product: Tower 28 SOS Daily Rescue Facial Spray
am.description:
Mist over clean, dry skin and let it dry fully before the next step. The entire ingredient list is water, salt, and hypochlorous acid, making this the tidy treatment step for redness, post-workout irritation, and blemish-prone sensitive skin.

Do not keep spraying just because it feels refreshing. Once or twice daily is plenty unless your dermatologist tells you otherwise.

am.title: Barrier Cream
am.description:
Apply one or two pumps after the SOS spray has dried. Ceramides, fatty acids, sterols, glycerin, and peptides make this the plush barrier-support step, and the formula is free of fragrance and essential oils.

It is rich. Combination or oily skin can use a thinner layer or swap to the lighter Skinfix Barrier Balancing Water Cream.

am.title: SPF Eye Cream
am.product: Supergoop Bright-Eyed 100% Mineral Eye Cream SPF 40
am.description:
Tap an even layer around the eye contour before face SPF. The fragrance-free mineral filters are a sensible sensitive-eye starting point, while the peach tint can visually brighten darkness but may not match every complexion.

The untinted, perfume-free Ultrasun Eye Protection SPF 30 is a European alternative. Patch test first and stop if either formula makes the eyes water or the lids burn.

Read my full glowing review on this product here.

am.title: Mineral SPF
am.product: Paula's Choice CALM Barrier Protect Mineral Sunscreen SPF 30
am.description:
Apply generously as the final step. This is a fragrance-free mineral sunscreen made for dry, redness-prone skin, with soothing allantoin and centella alongside the UV filters.

SPF 30 is the floor, not an excuse to apply a whisper-thin layer. If this stings or does not sit well, EltaMD UV Pure SPF 47 is a fragrance-free, all-mineral alternative, though it may look whiter on skin.

pm.title: Cleanse
pm.description: Cleanse once at night without a washcloth, brush, or hot water. Add a separate first cleanse only when makeup or water-resistant sunscreen actually requires it.

pm.title: Redness + Blemish Mist
pm.product: Tower 28 SOS Daily Rescue Facial Spray
pm.description: Mist over clean skin and give it a minute to dry. This is useful when sensitivity travels with redness or breakouts, but it is still optional on nights when skin already feels calm.

pm.title: Soothing Eye Cream
pm.product: Biossance Squalane + Marine Algae Eye Cream
pm.description:
Press a rice-grain amount around each eye before face cream. Squalane, panthenol, hyaluronic acid, antioxidants, and a peptide provide a richer cushion without fragrance, essential oils, retinoids, or exfoliating acids.

If the eye area is actively irritated, use fewer products—not more—and speak with a clinician about persistent eyelid dermatitis.

pm.title: Barrier Cream
pm.description: Finish with one or two pumps over the face and neck. There is no retinoid, peel, or exfoliating toner hiding elsewhere in this routine; the goal is to make the barrier feel boringly reliable before considering stronger treatment.

point_description: A minimalist medical-luxury routine with an eight-ingredient lipid serum, rich ceramide care, and sheer mineral SPF.

am.title: Cleanse
am.description:
Use a small amount with lukewarm water, then pat rather than rub. This is a soap-, sulfate-, fragrance-, and dye-free cleanser developed for sensitive or compromised skin.

As ever, water alone is a perfectly respectable morning cleanse when your barrier is already happy.

am.title: Lipid Serum
am.description:
Spread a pea-sized amount over clean skin. It has only eight ingredients: humectants, hyaluronic acid, a chelator, citric acid, and the brand's lipid-like TSC ingredient. This is luxury minimalism aimed at dehydration, redness, and stressed or post-procedure-feeling skin.

The ingredient list is elegant; the price is extravagant. Patch test it anyway, because expensive skin can still be sensitive skin.

am.title: Barrier Cream
am.description:
Apply a pea-sized layer after serum. Ceramide NP, glycerin, shea butter, meadowfoam oil, and fatty alcohols make this a rich barrier cream, while the formula avoids fragrance and essential oils.

Because it contains several plant oils and extracts, patch testing still matters. Use less—or skip it under SPF—if your skin is oily or congestion-prone.

am.title: SPF Eye Cream
am.product: Colorescience Total Eye 3-in-1 Renewal Therapy SPF 35
am.description:
Apply around the eye contour before face SPF. This all-mineral eye cream protects while color-correcting, hydrating, and softening the look of puffiness; the tint must genuinely match rather than being tolerated because the product is expensive.

For a fragrance-free untinted option, try Ultrasun Eye Protection SPF 30. Patch test either formula on reactive skin.

am.title: Mineral SPF
am.product: Colorescience Total Protection No-Show Mineral Sunscreen SPF 50
am.description:
Shake, apply generously, and give it a minute to set. This is an untinted, fragrance-free zinc sunscreen designed to blend more sheerly than traditional mineral formulas, with bisabolol and allantoin for added comfort.

No mineral sunscreen is visually invisible on every person. Blend in thin passes until you reach the full amount rather than stopping early to avoid cast.

pm.title: Cleanse
pm.description: Use as the nightly cleanse, massaging gently with fingertips and rinsing well. If makeup needs a first cleanse, choose a fragrance-free remover and keep this as the second, calming pass.

pm.title: Lipid Serum
pm.description: Apply another pea-sized amount over the face, with a separate drop for the neck if wanted. It is doing the treatment job here without retinoids, exfoliating acids, or a high-strength brightening active.

pm.title: Soothing Eye Cream
pm.description:
Pat a rice-grain amount around each eye before face cream. Purslane, panthenol, glycerin, macadamia oil, and other lipids make this a fragrance-free luxury hydration step rather than another aggressive active.

The elegant texture is the splurge; the useful job is still straightforward moisture. Patch test it, especially if nut-derived oils have bothered you before.

pm.title: Barrier Cream
pm.description: Finish with a comfortable layer over face and neck. This routine spends its money on texture and a very focused serum, but the underlying strategy is the same as the drugstore version: cleanse gently, hold onto water, and stop poking an already reactive barrier.

point_description: A sensitive, acne-prone, less-is-more routine built around Vanicream cleansing, clean towels, LED cooling, Hydrinity mist, Avène Cicalfate, SkinCeuticals SPF, and a source-backed nighttime double cleanse.

sources.summary: Allure reports her pregnancy skin constants as SkinCeuticals C E Ferulic and Purifying Cleanser, plus KORA body oil and weekly lymphatic massage.

sources.summary: Sofia says sensitive skin keeps her routine minimalist, names Nudescreen Daily Mineral SPF 30 as her go-to, and keeps Nudestix Hydra-Peptide Lip Butter in her purse.

sources.label: Vogue 2019
sources.headline: Sofia Richie on Sensitive Skin Care, Her Travel Routine, and the Beauty Lessons She's Learned From Her Dad
sources.summary: Her first Beauty Secrets routine centers sensitive-skin Lancer products, Mario Badescu rose spray, La Mer eye care, hydrating eye patches, and daily sunscreen.

am.title: Cleanse
am.description:
Wash with the bar cleanser in the morning. In her 2025 Vogue routine, Sofia says she uses Vanicream bar soap for her face because it is the only thing that does not break her out.

Earlier routines were different: Vogue 2019 showed Lancer The Method: Cleanse Sensitive Skin, Allure 2024 named SkinCeuticals Purifying Cleanser, and Vogue 2024 named SkinCeuticals Simply Clean.

am.title: Clean Towel
am.product: Clean Skin Club Clean Towels XL
am.description:
Pat dry after cleansing. In Vogue, Sofia says she uses these to dry her skin and has noticed the biggest difference when she avoids detergent residue from regular towels.

She says you can use anything, even a tissue; the idea is a clean, low-irritation dry-down.

am.title: LED + Cooling Mask
am.description:
Use on clean, dry skin. In Vogue, Sofia says she uses the Shark cryo mask for anti-aging, to help kill bacteria, and because the little fan keeps her cool.

This is a tool step, so it is not the five-minute rushed-mom version of the routine, but it fits her acne-and-rosacea-support logic.

am.title: Purifying Mist
am.description:
Mist after the LED mask. In Vogue, Sofia calls Hydrinity Hyacyn Active the hand sanitizer for your face because she likes it for keeping her skin feeling clean and calm.

In her older sensitive-skin routine, she used Mario Badescu Facial Spray with Aloe, Herbs and Rosewater after moisturizer.

am.title: Barrier Cream
am.description:
Warm it between your hands first, then press it in. Sofia calls Avène Cicalfate her holy grail in Vogue and says it looks glowier and more gorgeous the more you warm it into the skin.

Older source-backed moisturizers include Lancer The Method: Nourish Sensitive Skin, EltaMD AM Therapy Facial Moisturizer Lotion, and SkinCeuticals Triple Lipid Restore 2:4:2.

am.title: SPF
am.product: SkinCeuticals Physical Fusion UV Defense SPF 50
am.description:
Apply as the final daytime skin step. In Vogue 2025, Sofia calls this her SkinCeuticals 50 sunscreen and says it does not break her out and only does good things.

NewBeauty previously had her using Nudescreen Daily Mineral Veil SPF 30 every day, and Vogue 2019 showed a Supergoop Glow Stick SPF before makeup.

am.title: Lip Occlusive
am.description:
Use on lips whenever they need a thick protective layer. In Vogue, Sofia calls Aquaphor her lip holy grail and says she cannot live without her enormous tub.

NewBeauty also says she keeps Nudestix Hydra-Peptide Lip Butter in her purse, while Marie Claire's pregnancy-product list included Summer Fridays Lip Butter Balm.

pm.title: Cleansing Balm
pm.product: NUDESKIN Citrus Clean Balm & Makeup Melt
pm.description:
Use as the makeup-melting first cleanse on nights she wore makeup or SPF. Goss.ie, citing Sofia's Byrdie routine, says she double cleanses every night so all her makeup is off.

Massage onto dry skin, rinse or remove with a damp cloth, then follow with the gel cleanser.

pm.title: Double Cleanse
pm.description:
Follow the cleansing balm with this gel cleanser. Goss.ie reports that Sofia used NUDESKIN Citrus Cleansing Balm and Makeup Melt plus Gentle Face Hydra-Gel Cleanser for a super-clean double cleanse.

Keep the cleanse gentle; her sources repeat that she has sensitive, oily, acne-prone skin and prefers a less-is-more routine.

pm.title: Exfoliating Pads
pm.description:
Swipe over clean skin only on breakout-prone areas, and do not scrub. Allure's 2023 interview says Sofia used Christie Kidd Perfect Skin Fresh Pads in the morning, and the brand's directions say to sweep gently over blemish areas once or twice daily.

This is an acne/oil-control step rather than an every-skin, every-night requirement.

pm.title: Vitamin C
pm.description:
Use as the antioxidant-brightening serum. Allure says Sofia calls C E Ferulic one of the two constants in her morning and night regimens during pregnancy, and Vogue's SkinCeuticals feature keeps it central to her routine.

If using it twice daily is too much, make it a morning step and keep night focused on cleanse and barrier care.

pm.title: Hydrating Serum
pm.description: Apply before moisturizer when skin needs more cushion. Vogue's SkinCeuticals product lineup and Sofia bundle include H.A. Intensifier as the hydrating serum step, with the SkinCeuticals routine placing it morning and night.

pm.title: Moisturizer
pm.description:
Use after serum as the richer night moisturizer. In the SkinCeuticals Sofia routine, Dr. Mamina recommends Triple Lipid Restore 2:4:2 to support the barrier and smooth texture.

This is the more treatment-cream version of the simpler Avène Cicalfate step she uses in her 2025 Vogue routine.

pm.title: Lip Balm
pm.description:
Finish with lip balm. NewBeauty says Sofia never goes anywhere without Nudestix Hydra-Peptide Lip Butter to keep her lips moisturized 24/7.

For a thicker bedtime seal, her newer Vogue routine points back to Aquaphor Healing Ointment.

point_description: A natural-leaning model routine built around makeup-removal wipes, Tata Harper cleansing and essence, KORA vitamin C, rich moisturizers, masks, peel pads, and lip balm.

sources.headline: Watch Lily Aldridge Share Her Nightly Skin Care Routine
sources.summary: Her Go to Bed With Me routine lists RMS wipes, Shiva Rose balm, Dr. Dennis Gross peel pads, Tatcha masks, KORA vitamin C, Dr. Barbara Sturm serum, Weleda Skin Food, Windsor Edwards lip balm, and Tata Harper eye balm.

sources.headline: Lily Aldridge, Model
sources.summary: Aldridge describes her nursing-era quick and luxurious routines, including Burt's Bees or RMS wipes, Tata Harper cleanser and essence, KORA vitamin C, Tata Harper moisturizers, and Windsor Edwards lip balm.

sources.summary: Her pregnancy Beauty Secrets routine includes Fresh Lotus Rescue Mask, Hatch Belly Mask, Naturopathica Manuka Honey Cleansing Balm, ReFa roller, KORA moisturizer, Windsor Edwards balm, Kate McLeod Mama Stone, RMS concealer, and Noni Glow Face Oil.

sources.summary: Vogue says Aldridge focuses on moisturized skin with Heritage Store rosewater mist, RMS coconut oil wipes, and La Mer as her skin-care luxury.
