sources.summary: Aldridge discusses pregnancy-linked natural-product discoveries, coconut and jojoba body oils, Windsor Edwards lip balm, RMS Un Cover-Up, and nightly bath rituals.

sources.label: Vogue 2014
sources.headline: #IWokeUpLikeThis: Lily Aldridge Reveals the Strategies Behind Her Morning Routine
sources.summary: Her earlier morning routine included Proactiv Deep Cleansing Wash, rosewater toner, KORA Organics Day and Night Cream, La Mer The Eye Concentrate, and regular exfoliation.

am.title: Makeup Reset
am.product: RMS Beauty Ultimate Makeup Remover Wipes
am.description:
Use as the first pass when there is makeup left from the night before or a rushed morning. Into The Gloss says Lily starts by taking makeup off because she is often too tired to do it at night, choosing Burt's Bees wipes or RMS coconut wipes when there is more makeup.

Harper's Bazaar also starts her nighttime routine with RMS Beauty wipes, so these get the more recent display spot.

am.title: Cleanse
am.description:
Massage on after makeup removal and remove with a warm towel. Into The Gloss says Lily uses Tata Harper's scrubby cleanser in her more luxurious daytime routine.

In an older Vogue morning routine, she used Proactiv Deep Cleansing Wash, but the Tata Harper cleanser is the newer source-backed skin-care routine cleanser.

am.title: Essence
am.description:
Swipe on with a cotton ball after cleansing. Lily tells Into The Gloss this takes off leftover dirt and makes her skin shiny.

This is the glow-and-polish step, so use less often if skin feels sensitive.

am.title: Vitamin C
am.product: KORA Organics Kakadu Plum Vitamin C Serum
am.description:
Apply after essence as the vitamin C step. Into The Gloss says Lily maybe uses a vitamin C serum from KORA Organics, and Harper's Bazaar later lists KORA Noni Bright Vitamin C Serum in her nighttime product lineup.

Noni Bright has since been replaced by KORA's current Kakadu Plum Vitamin C Serum, so this links the newer same-brand vitamin C.

am.title: Moisturizer
am.description:
Use as the daytime moisturizer. Into The Gloss says Lily uses Tata Harper Repairative Moisturizer, and her older Vogue morning routine also emphasized seasonal moisturizers.

Earlier source-backed options include La Mer The Moisturizing Soft Cream as her big skin-care luxury and KORA Organics Day and Night Cream, which is no longer reliably available.

am.title: Lip Balm
am.description: Use on lips whenever they feel dry. Vogue says Windsor Edwards lip balm is addictive for her, Vogue 2018 quotes her saying she uses it pregnant or not, and Into The Gloss calls it a sustainable favorite.

pm.title: Remove Makeup
pm.product: RMS Beauty Ultimate Makeup Remover Wipes
pm.description: Start by removing makeup. Harper's Bazaar says Lily begins her nighttime routine with RMS Beauty wipes infused with coconut oil, and Into The Gloss says she reaches for RMS coconut wipes when there is a lot of makeup.

pm.title: Cleansing Balm
pm.description:
Massage onto skin, then remove with a warm washcloth. Vogue's pregnancy routine shows Lily double cleansing off the mask with Naturopathica's Manuka Honey Cleansing Balm and saying it leaves skin shiny and supple.

Use this as the balm-cleanse option when wipes are not enough.

pm.title: Glow Balm
pm.description: Use a light layer when skin wants a glowy balm moment. Harper's Bazaar says Lily smears on Shiva Rose Glow Face Balm and jokes that anything with balm and glow in the name has her sold. (Honestly, same.)

pm.title: Peel Pads
pm.product: Dr. Dennis Gross Alpha Beta Universal Daily Peel
pm.description:
Use only occasionally, not automatically every night. Harper's Bazaar lists Dr. Dennis Gross Alpha Beta Universal Daily Peel in her nighttime routine product lineup.

This is the exfoliating acid step, so skip it when skin is irritated or when using another active mask.

pm.title: Eye Mask
pm.product: Tatcha Deep Hydration Revitalizing Eye Mask
pm.description:
Use when eyes look tired or travel-worn. Harper's Bazaar lists Tatcha Deep Hydration Revitalizing Eye Mask in her nighttime routine.

Vogue France also notes that she liked Shiseido eye masks for travel, but those pure-retinol eye masks are discontinued and not the priority here.

pm.title: Sheet Mask
pm.description:
Use as an occasional hydration mask when skin needs extra glow. Harper's Bazaar lists Tatcha Luminous Dewy Skin Mask in Lily's routine.

In Vogue's pregnancy routine, she used Fresh Lotus Youth Preserve Rescue Mask and joked about her daughter saying she had barnacles on her face.

pm.title: Vitamin C
pm.product: KORA Organics Kakadu Plum Vitamin C Serum
pm.description:
Apply after cleansing or masking. Harper's Bazaar lists KORA Noni Bright Vitamin C Serum in her PM routine, and Into The Gloss says she uses a KORA vitamin C serum in her more luxurious routine.

Noni Bright has been replaced by Kakadu Plum Vitamin C Serum, so this is the current same-brand vitamin C link.

pm.title: Serum
pm.product: Dr. Barbara Sturm Super Anti-Aging Serum
pm.description: Use as the luxury serum step after vitamin C or instead of it on simpler nights. Harper's Bazaar names Dr. Barbara Sturm's Super Anti-Aging Serum as one of Lily's nighttime favorites.

pm.title: Rich Cream
pm.product: Weleda Skin Food Original Ultra-Rich Cream
pm.description: Use as the rich comfort cream when skin is dry. Harper's Bazaar lists Weleda Skin Food in her routine, while Into The Gloss says Lily uses Tata Harper's Crème Riche at night and keeps it next to her bed.

pm.title: Eye Balm
pm.product: Tata Harper Boosted Contouring Eye Balm
pm.description:
Tap around the eye area as a final targeted step. Harper's Bazaar lists Tata Harper Boosted Contouring Eye Balm in Lily's nighttime routine.

Her older Vogue morning routine also named La Mer The Eye Concentrate as part of her routine.

pm.title: Lip Balm
pm.description: Finish with the same lip balm she keeps returning to. Harper's Bazaar, Vogue, and Into The Gloss all connect Lily to Windsor Edwards Lip Balm, and she says she uses it pregnant or not.

point_description: A forgiving first routine: one cleanser, one optional barrier serum, moisturizer, and a high-protection sunscreen you can actually wear every day.

am.title: Cleanse
am.description:
Massage a small amount over damp skin and rinse with lukewarm water. It removes oil, makeup, and everyday sunscreen without making a beginner buy a separate product for every cleansing scenario.

If your face feels dry but clean when you wake up, rinse with water instead. If you are consistently very oily, the CeraVe Foaming Facial Cleanser is the better match.

am.title: Optional Barrier Serum
am.product: The Ordinary Soothing & Barrier Support Serum
am.description:
Apply a few drops before moisturizer. The 2% niacinamide, ceramides, and soothing ingredients give a new routine some help with dehydration, visible redness, uneven texture, and barrier support without jumping straight to a peel or retinoid.

This step is optional. Start once daily for the first week, and skip it entirely if cleanser, moisturizer, and SPF are all your skin needs.

am.title: Moisturize
am.description:
Use one or two pumps over slightly damp skin. Despite the PM on the bottle, this lightweight, fragrance-free lotion works perfectly well morning or night; ceramides, hyaluronic acid, and niacinamide cover the basic hydration and barrier job.

If sunscreen is moisturizing enough on its own, combination or oily skin can skip this in the morning.

am.title: Eye-Area SPF
am.product: Cetaphil Sheer Mineral Sunscreen Stick SPF 50
am.description:
Glide the stick onto a clean fingertip, then tap a generous, even layer around the orbital bone and upper eye contour before face SPF. This fragrance-free drugstore mineral SPF 50 is specifically intended for use around the eyes and is easier to place precisely than a runny face sunscreen.

It is an eye-area sunscreen, not a treatment eye cream; the BYOMA eye gel at night covers the hydration step. Keep it out of the eyes and off the lash line, and expect some possible mineral cast.

am.title: SPF
am.product: Neutrogena Invisible Daily Defense Face Serum SPF 60+
am.description:
Apply generously as the last morning step to the face, ears, and neck, then reapply when outdoors. This is the habit with the biggest long-term payoff: broad-spectrum SPF 60+, an invisible finish, and 80 minutes of water resistance.

If chemical filters sting, try the untinted, all-mineral Blue Lizard Sensitive Face Mineral Sunscreen SPF 50+. It may leave more cast, so do not solve that by applying less.

pm.title: Cleanse
pm.description: Cleanse for about 30 to 60 seconds, then rinse well. One cleanse is enough most nights; add a separate first cleanse only when heavy makeup or water-resistant sunscreen is still hanging around.

pm.title: Optional Barrier Serum
pm.product: The Ordinary Soothing & Barrier Support Serum
pm.description:
Use a few drops after cleansing if you skipped it in the morning or want more hydration. There is no need to use it twice daily just to finish the bottle faster.

If persistent acne is the real concern, this soothing serum is not an acne medication. A dermatologist can help, or consider Differin Adapalene Gel 0.1% instead, starting only two nights a week and avoiding it during pregnancy.

pm.title: Cooling Eye Gel
pm.description:
Use one small pump across both eye contours before moisturizer. Ceramides, cholesterol, multiple forms of hyaluronic acid, and a vitamin C derivative give a beginner hydration and temporary de-puffing without introducing a retinoid.

The cooling ingredients can feel refreshing but are not mandatory. Stop if the eye area tingles or waters; a basic moisturizer is the backup plan, not a skincare failure.

pm.title: Moisturize
pm.description: Finish with one or two pumps. Give the routine about a month before adding another active unless something is irritating you; consistency tells you far more than changing products every few days.

point_description: The same beginner-friendly foundation in nicer textures, with a restrained 5% niacinamide serum for oiliness, redness, and uneven texture.

am.title: Cleanse
am.product: Skinfix Barrier+ Ceramide + Ectoin Hydrating Gentle Gel Cleanser
am.description:
Massage a small amount over damp skin and rinse. This is the pleasant-texture upgrade: a gentle gel designed to remove daily buildup without the tight, squeaky finish that often sends beginners scrambling for more products.

Dry skin can simply rinse with water in the morning and save the cleanser for night.

am.title: Optional Niacinamide
am.product: Kiehl's Ultra Pure High-Potency 5% Niacinamide Serum
am.description:
Apply two or three drops before moisturizer, either all over or only through oily, redness-prone areas. Five percent niacinamide is a sensible middle ground for excess oil, the look of pores, redness, and uneven texture without starting at the internet-favorite 10% or 20% end of the pool.

Begin once daily. If your skin is already happy, this is optional rather than a tax for being in your 20s.

am.title: Moisturize
am.description:
Smooth on a light layer while skin is slightly damp. Glycerin and squalane make this a straightforward daily moisturizer with a more polished texture than the drugstore option.

If you run oily, the lighter Skinfix Barrier Balancing Water Cream is a better swap, or skip moisturizer under a sufficiently hydrating sunscreen.

am.title: SPF Eye Cream
am.product: Supergoop Bright-Eyed 100% Mineral Eye Cream SPF 40
am.description:
Tap an even layer around the eye contour before face sunscreen. The dedicated mineral SPF 40 formula is more controlled around the eyes than the clear face SPF, and its light peach tint can help visually brighten darkness.

If the tint does not work for you, use the untinted, fragrance-free Ultrasun Eye Protection SPF 30.

Read my full glowing review on this product here.

am.title: SPF
am.description:
Apply generously as the final morning step. The clear gel disappears across skin tones and wears like a primer, which matters because the best sunscreen is the one you will use in the proper amount every day.

If you prefer an untinted mineral formula, try Paula's Choice CALM Barrier Protect Mineral Sunscreen SPF 30. Mineral does not automatically mean irritation-proof, so patch test whichever formula you choose.

pm.title: Cleanse
pm.product: Skinfix Barrier+ Ceramide + Ectoin Hydrating Gentle Gel Cleanser
pm.description: Massage over wet skin, rinse, and pat dry. It can remove everyday SPF and light makeup; use a separate first cleanse only when it genuinely leaves something behind.

pm.title: Optional Niacinamide
pm.product: Kiehl's Ultra Pure High-Potency 5% Niacinamide Serum
pm.description:
Use two or three drops after cleansing if evening is your preferred treatment time. More is not better, and twice-daily use is unnecessary if once daily is working.

For ongoing acne, painful breakouts, or scarring, see a dermatologist rather than building an expensive tower of serums.

pm.title: Hydrating Eye Cream
pm.product: Kiehl's Creamy Eye Treatment with Avocado
pm.description:
Warm a rice-grain amount between fingertips, then tap it around each eye before moisturizer. The fragrance-free water-in-oil cream focuses on all-night hydration and the look of dry fine lines rather than giving a new skincare user another active to manage.

It is rich, so use very little and switch to a lighter gel if you are prone to milia.

pm.title: Moisturize
pm.description: Finish with a comfortable layer. Keep this routine unchanged for about four weeks unless something irritates you; only then decide whether you actually need a concern-specific active.

point_description: A prevention-first French pharmacy routine with a mineral-water mist, cica hydration, 15% cosmetic azelaic acid, and a matte SPF for acne-prone skin.

am.title: Cleanse
am.description:
Use a small amount with lukewarm water, or just rinse if your face feels clean and dry in the morning. This is the French-market name for the Sensibio foaming gel: soap-free, fragrance-free, and pleasantly unexciting.

Very oily skin can swap to Bioderma Sébium Gel Moussant, but there is no need to buy the acid-based Active version just because it exists.

am.title: Optional Mineral-Water Mist
am.description:
Mist after cleansing when you want a fresh, slightly damp base for serum or moisturizer, then press it in and continue while skin is still damp. This is essentially beautifully packaged French mineral water, not an active treatment, but the very fine spray is genuinely nice during travel, heat, or an over-air-conditioned workday.

Do not let repeated layers of water evaporate on bare skin and expect them to moisturize on their own; follow with the next hydrating step.

am.title: Cica Serum
am.product: Uriage Bariéderm-CICA Daily Intensive Repairing Serum
am.description:
Apply a few drops before moisturizer. This is the useful extra step for dehydration, post-breakout irritation, and a barrier that gets cranky from weather, travel, or trying too many products.

It is fragrance- and alcohol-free, but still optional. In your 20s, sunscreen consistency matters more than collecting serums.

am.title: Moisturize
am.description:
Use a small amount over slightly damp skin. This is the fragrance-free sibling of the cult Lait-Crème Concentré, with a comfortable satin finish that works well under sunscreen.

It contains shea butter and beeswax, so oily skin may prefer the lighter Uriage Bariéderm-CICA Daily Gel-Cream.

Read why the original cult cream won me over here.

am.title: Untinted SPF Eye Cream
am.description:
Tap carefully around the lower and upper eye contour before face SPF. This Swiss pharmacy cream-gel is the honest regional choice because true French eye creams with tested SPF are unusually scarce; it is untinted, perfume-free, water-resistant, and ophthalmologist-tested.

U.S. shoppers can use the mineral, lightly peach-tinted Supergoop Bright-Eyed SPF 40 instead.

Read my full glowing review on this product here.

am.title: French SPF
am.product: Eucerin Sun Oil Control Gel-Cream SPF 50+
am.description:
Apply generously as the final morning step, including ears and neck. The untinted gel-cream is the 20s pick because it is quick-drying, non-greasy, and designed for oily or acne-prone skin—the kind of texture that makes daily SPF easier to keep doing.

The Eucerin tinted Oil Control SPF 50+ adds pigment for visible-light protection and a little complexion evening, although its limited shade needs to match. For an untinted mineral alternative, try Uriage Bariésun Mineral Cream SPF 50+, with the usual warning that mineral formulas can leave a cast.

pm.title: Cleanse
pm.description: Massage over wet skin and rinse well. If makeup or water-resistant SPF remains, use the iconic Bioderma Créaline H2O first, then follow with this gel rather than rubbing harder with cotton.

pm.title: Optional Zinc Mist
pm.description:
On oily, post-workout, or razor-irritated days, mist over clean skin, let it settle, and continue with the rest of the routine. The formula is wonderfully French-pharmacy simple—water, zinc sulfate, and sodium chloride—and makes a more purposeful alternative to the Evian mist when shine and superficial irritation are the issue.

This is an optional comfort step, not an acne medication. Skip it if it feels drying, and do not expect zinc water to replace the azelaic-acid treatment.

pm.title: 15% Azelaic Acid
pm.description:
Use a pea-size amount two or three nights a week after cleansing, then build toward nightly use only if skin stays comfortable. This is the especially good French-pharmacy find for breakouts, post-blemish marks, uneven tone, and redness: a cosmetic formula with 15% azelaic acid, whereas U.S. non-prescription products are usually 10% and 15% medicinal azelaic acid is prescription-only there.

This is not the same as buying the French medicines Finacea 15% or Skinoren 20% without a prescription—both are prescription products in France. Azéane is the freely sold cosmetic option. It can still sting or pill, so introduce it slowly and ask the pharmacist or a dermatologist about persistent acne or rosacea.

Read my full review on this product here.

pm.title: Cica Serum
pm.product: Uriage Bariéderm-CICA Daily Intensive Repairing Serum
pm.description: Repeat the serum when skin feels dehydrated or irritated. There is deliberately no automatic retinoid here; a healthy 20-something routine does not need to behave like an emergency anti-aging intervention.

pm.title: Sensitive-Eye Cream
pm.description:
Smooth a rice-grain amount around each eye before moisturizer. The fragrance-free French pharmacy formula combines barrier hydration with caffeine and a peptide for the look of puffiness, dark circles, and early fine lines without adding retinal to the 20s routine.

It is sold internationally, but France is the fun place to look for local pricing and pharmacy promotions; the formula itself is not stronger there.

pm.title: Moisturize
pm.description: Finish with a comfortable layer. Use more on dry areas and less through the T-zone. If active acne is the main concern, treat that separately with a dermatologist or pharmacist instead of hoping a richer French cream will fix it.

point_description: A brightening and early-correction routine pairing French vitamin C, retinal, barrier cream, and the cult UVMune 400 sunscreen without piling on exfoliants.

am.title: Cleanse
am.description: Massage over dry or damp skin and remove gently according to the label. A stronger treatment routine needs a boring, fragrance-free cleanser, not an exfoliating face wash competing for attention.

am.title: Vitamin C
am.description:
Apply a small amount to dry skin before moisturizer. This French ampoule uses 20% optimized vitamin C for dullness, uneven tone, and antioxidant support.

It also contains alcohol and fragrance, so start every other morning and do not force it if it stings. Sensitive skin can choose the gentler Uriage Bariéderm-CICA Daily Serum instead.

am.title: Barrier Cream
am.description:
Apply a thin layer after vitamin C. This is the calm, fragrance-free buffer in the routine, keeping hydration steady while the treatment steps do their work.

If your sunscreen supplies enough moisture, combination skin can skip this in the morning and keep it for night.

am.title: Untinted SPF Eye Cream
am.description:
Tap around the upper and lower eye contour before UVMune. The untinted, perfume-free cream-gel is ophthalmologist-tested and gives this easily missed area its own labeled broad-spectrum SPF without adding another tint.

For a U.S. mineral option, use the lightly peach-tinted Supergoop Bright-Eyed SPF 40.

Read my full glowing review on this product here.

am.title: French SPF
am.product: La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVMune 400 Invisible Fluid SPF 50+
am.description:
Shake well and apply generously as the final morning step, including ears and neck. This is the cult French-pharmacy sunscreen worth looking for specifically in France: the untinted, fragrance-free European formula uses Mexoryl 400 for protection through the ultra-long UVA range, which is especially relevant when the goal is preventing additional pigment and collagen damage.

The texture is very fluid and contains a substantial amount of alcohol, so dry or reactive skin may prefer Bioderma Photoderm SPOT-AGE SPF 50+. The tinted UVMune 400 Fluid adds pigment if its shade works for you; Avène Mineral Fluid SPF 50+ is the untinted mineral alternative.

pm.title: Cleanse
pm.description: Remove makeup and sunscreen without scrubbing, then cleanse once. A micellar-water first pass is useful when needed, but double cleansing is not a nightly moral obligation.

pm.title: Optional Beauty Mist
pm.description:
On recovery nights, shake and mist after cleansing for the classic French-pharmacy ritual, then let it settle before moisturizer. I would buy this for the refreshing, sensorial experience—not because a mist is going to remodel collagen or replace a serum.

Beauty Elixir contains alcohol, fragrance, and several essential oils. Skip it if you are sensitive, rosacea-prone, pregnant, or using retinal that night; Caudalie's gentler Grape Water is the better fragrance-free alternative.

pm.title: Post-Procedure / First-Aid Extra
pm.description:
Keep this as the post-procedure or superficially damaged-skin option rather than another nightly layer. Use it on the affected area when skin is recovering from a superficial peel, laser treatment, healed tattoo, or minor irritation, following the clinician's aftercare instructions; on those nights, skip Beauty Elixir, vitamin C, and retinal.

For a small superficial burn or localized sunburn, the cult French medicine-cabinet product is BiafineAct. Cool a fresh burn under cool running tap water first and ask the pharmacist how to use it. Biafine is not sunscreen or a daily moisturizer. Do not self-treat an infected or bleeding lesion with it; blistering, extensive burns or burns involving the face, hands, feet, genitals, or major joints need medical assessment.

pm.title: Retinal Night Cream
pm.product: Avène Hyaluron Activ B3 Multi-Intensive Night Cream
pm.description:
Start one or two nights a week, using the pump dose over dry skin and avoiding eyelids, lip edges, and nose creases. The French formula combines retinal, niacinamide, and hyaluronic acid for fine lines, firmness, and uneven tone.

It contains fragrance and may tingle. Do not layer it with another retinoid or exfoliating acid, and avoid retinoids during pregnancy.

pm.title: Triple-Correction Eye Cream
pm.product: Avène Hyaluron Activ B3 Triple Action Eye Cream
pm.description:
Tap a rice-grain amount around each eye before barrier cream. Six percent niacinamide, hyaluronic acid, dextran sulfate, and adenosine target hydration, puffiness, and early lines without adding a second retinal product beside the night cream.

The U.S. and European versions are available, while French pharmacies may offer better pricing or sets. Check the box rather than assuming every similarly named Avène eye product has the same formula.

pm.title: Barrier Cream
pm.description: Finish with a thin layer, or apply it before and after retinal if you need a moisturizer sandwich. On non-retinal nights, cleanser and this cream are enough.

point_description: A richer mature-skin routine with a soothing thermal mist, plumping hydration, lipid support, 0.1% retinal, and an anti-photoaging SPF fluid.

am.title: Cream Cleanse
am.description:
Massage a generous amount over the face and remove gently according to the label directions. This very short, fragrance-free formula cleans without asking drier mature skin to tolerate foam for the sake of feeling clean.

In the morning, water alone is also completely respectable.

am.title: Soothing Thermal Mist
am.description:
Mist after cleansing when skin feels warm, tight, or reactive, gently press away excess, and follow promptly with serum or cream. This is the soothing mist in the group and the one I would choose for drier mature skin or a barrier made touchy by travel and treatment.

It is optional comfort, not a moisturizer by itself. Sealing it in matters more than repeatedly spraying water and letting it evaporate.

am.title: Plumping Serum
am.product: Vichy Liftactiv H.A. Epidermic Filler Serum
am.description:
Press a few drops over slightly damp skin. The fragrance-free formula combines hyaluronic acid with a vitamin C derivative for temporary plumping, hydration, and support around fine lines without turning the morning routine into an active obstacle course.

For skin specifically changing through peri- or post-menopause, Vichy Neovadiol Meno 5 Bi-Serum is the more targeted French-pharmacy alternative, but it contains exfoliating acids and fragrance.

am.title: Rich Moisturizer
am.description:
Use a thin layer over serum, concentrating on areas that feel dry. Shea butter, babassu oil, peptides, and hyaluronic acid make this a proper comfort cream for mature skin rather than a weightless gel pretending everyone wants the same texture.

It is fragranced. If that is a problem, replace it with the simpler Avène Tolérance Control Balm.

am.title: Untinted SPF Eye Cream
am.description:
Once the treatment eye cream has settled, tap this around the lower and upper eye contour before face SPF. The untinted, perfume-free Swiss pharmacy cream-gel is ophthalmologist-tested and gives mature eye-area skin its own labeled broad-spectrum protection.

U.S. shoppers can choose the mineral, lightly peach-tinted Supergoop Bright-Eyed SPF 40. If two eye layers pill, use the SPF eye cream alone in the morning and keep DermAbsolu for night.

Read my full glowing review on this product here.

am.title: Hydrating French SPF
am.product: Vichy Capital Soleil UV-Age Daily SPF 50+
am.description:
Apply generously as the final morning step. This untinted fluid is the 50s+ pick because the very light sunscreen film also includes niacinamide and peptides aimed at spots, dullness, and loss of firmness. A fluid can be easier to apply in the proper amount than stacking a very rich second cream over the moisturizer already here.

It contains alcohol and fragrance, so reactive skin should choose the fragrance-free La Roche-Posay UVMune 400 Hydrating Cream SPF 50+. The tinted UV-Age Daily is the visible-light option if its shade works; Bioderma Photoderm Mineral Fluid SPF 50+ is the untinted mineral alternative.

pm.title: Cream Cleanse
pm.description: Use enough product to lift sunscreen and makeup without friction. If heavy eye makeup remains, remove that separately rather than repeatedly wiping the whole face.

pm.title: 0.1% Retinal
pm.product: Avène Hyaluron Activ Procedure Lifting Cream 0.1% Retinal
pm.description:
Start one night a week, then move to two nights only after skin stays comfortable. This newer French 0.1% retinal cream is the stronger correction step for established lines, uneven texture, and loss of firmness.

Do not use it on the same night as exfoliating acids, and avoid retinoids during pregnancy. If you are new to vitamin A, begin with the gentler Hyaluron Activ B3 Night Cream from the 30s–40s routine.

pm.title: Recontouring Eye Cream
pm.description:
Tap a rice-grain amount around each eye after the face treatment and before moisturizer. The richer eye cream supports dryness and the temporary look of smoothness without adding another retinal product beside the 0.1% face treatment.

If the eye area becomes reactive, stop the retinal near it and use only this comfort step until skin is calm.

pm.title: Rich Moisturizer
pm.description: Finish with a comfortable layer, especially on retinal nights. If you prefer a dedicated night texture, the linked SVR Densitium Night Balm is the same age-focused idea in a more enveloping formula.

pm.title: Optional Lip Repair
pm.description:
Finish with a thin layer on chapped, fissured, or treatment-dry lips. This is the practical choice for a mature-skin routine because it is designed for irritated lips and small localized dry areas.

For the more fun cult purchase, swap in Nuxe Rêve de Miel Lip Balm as an overnight lip mask. It contains fragrance, citrus oils, honey, propolis, and beeswax, so Cicalfate is the safer pick for reactive lips or allergies.

point_description: A glow-and-redness routine built from Vogue's named products plus facialist-backed iS Clinical context: cleanse, mist, vitamin C, eye cream, cooling massage, sunscreen, and tinted SPF.

sources.headline: Watch Grimes Do Her Pregnancy Skin Care and Psychedelic Makeup Routine
sources.summary: Vogue names Grimes's iS Clinical vitamin C serum, Shangpree eye cream, rose quartz roller, Bioré sunscreen, and NARS tinted moisturizer.

sources.label: The L.A. Facialist 2020
sources.headline: CR Fashion Book: Meet the Facialist Who Keeps Grimes' Skin Glowing
sources.summary: Grimes's facialist Candace Marino says she was on a full iS Clinical regimen and describes monthly lymphatic massage, LED, oxygen dome, light lactic peels, and jelly masks.

sources.headline: The 6 weirdest things we learned from Grimes's pregnancy beauty routine
sources.summary: Dazed recaps the skin-care structure as cleanser, mist, Korean essence, vitamin C serum, sunscreen, and cooling massage with ice or a rose quartz roller.

sources.label: PAPER 2020
sources.headline: Grimes' Beauty Routine Is Exactly What You Think
sources.summary: PAPER confirms the same core products from the Vogue routine and highlights her iS Clinical serum, Shangpree eye cream, roller, and Bioré sunscreen.

am.title: Cleanse
am.description:
Start by washing the face. Vogue does not name Grimes's cleanser, but her facialist says Grimes was on a full iS Clinical regimen, so this links the brand's Cleansing Complex as the cleanser-context match rather than a product Grimes named on camera.

iS Clinical says to massage a small amount over damp face and neck, rinse thoroughly, and pat dry.

am.title: Mist
am.description:
Spritz after cleansing. In Vogue, Grimes says she usually uses a mist, but does not name the bottle; this is linked from iS Clinical because her facialist says she was on the brand's full regimen.

She also follows with an unnamed Korean essence that she says helped with redness and pregnancy skin problems. Since Vogue does not identify it, I won't assume a replacement.

am.title: Vitamin C
am.description:
Apply a thin layer after hydrating steps. Vogue identifies this as iS Clinical's brightening vitamin C serum, and Grimes says she likes vitamin C because she had heard it helps protect from the sun.

Let it settle before eye cream and sunscreen so the routine does not turn into a slippery stack.

am.title: Eye Cream
am.product: Peach & Lily Pure Radiance Brightening Eye Cream
am.description:
Tap a tiny amount around the eye area. Vogue says Grimes used Shangpree S-Energy Repair Eye Cream imported from Korea and said it keeps her looking fresh and youthful.

The Shangpree eye cream is not reliably available now, so this links a current Peach & Lily Korean eye cream instead.

am.title: Cool + Roll
am.product: Sephora Collection Rose Quartz Facial Roller
am.description:
Use the roller after serum and eye cream for a quick cooling massage. Vogue shows her using a rose quartz roller, and Dazed notes that she also uses ice on her face before shoots or stage moments to calm redness.

Roll gently rather than dragging; the goal is de-puffing and chill-vibes skin, not a workout for your face.

am.title: Sunscreen
am.product: Bioré UV Aqua Rich Watery Essence SPF 50
am.description: Apply generously as the true SPF layer. Vogue says Grimes really likes this Japanese version of this sunscreen because it has almost no texture, and she says you can never really have too much sunscreen.

am.title: Tinted SPF
am.product: NARS Pure Radiant Tinted Moisturizer SPF 30
am.description:
Use as the sheer tint step when she wants chill daytime coverage. Vogue says she adds NARS Pure Radiant Tinted Moisturizer after the Bioré sunscreen, and in the video she describes it as the regular-day layer when she is not going harder with makeup.

Treat this as coverage with SPF, not a replacement for the dedicated sunscreen underneath.

point_description: A minimal natural-leaning routine built around coconut oil, Luzern Force De Vie moisturizer, homemade face oil, mineral SPF, RMS balm, and bath/scrub rituals.

sources.summary: A current profile places Li in her 40s and frames The Afterparty around aging, motherhood, performance, and reinvention.

sources.headline: How Lykke Li Does Pregnancy: Crime Shows, Sushi Cravings, and Her Favorite Natural Face Oil
sources.summary: Li describes switching to natural products, using Luzern Force De Vie, Suntegrity mineral sunscreen, coconut oil, homemade face oils, bath rituals, and RMS balm.

sources.label: Coveteur 2014
sources.headline: Lykke Li
sources.summary: Coveteur captures Li's backstage beauty essentials: Dr. Hauschka face cream, RMS balms, coconut oil as moisturizer and makeup remover, and a very simple pre-show routine.

am.title: Oil-Based Cleanse
am.description:
Use as a low-maintenance oil cleanse or makeup-removing step when skin needs it. Coveteur quotes Lykke saying coconut oil is amazing: she uses it as moisturizer, in her hair, and to take off makeup.

Vogue also says she removes heavy show or event makeup with coconut oil first. If coconut oil clogs your skin, treat this as a source-backed Lykke step rather than universal advice.

am.title: Moisturize
am.product: Luzern Force De Vie Crème Luxe
am.description:
Apply after cleansing while skin is still comfortable and slightly damp. Vogue says Lykke uses Luzern Labs's Force De Vie moisturizing cream, and she dots her homemade face oil into it in the morning.

Luzern's current Force De Vie Crème Luxe is the closest current link for that moisturizer family.

am.title: Homemade Face Oil
am.description:
Use a few drops, either alone or mixed into moisturizer. Vogue says Lykke's homemade face oil includes avocado, grape seed, lavender, neroli, and jojoba oils, and that she had always used almond and coconut oil before experimenting with blends.

The linked avocado oil is just one accessible base oil from her recipe; other named ingredients include grape seed oil, jojoba oil, lavender oil, and neroli oil.

am.title: Mineral SPF
am.product: Suntegrity 5-in-1 Natural Moisturizing Face Sunscreen SPF 30
am.description:
Pat on as the last daytime skin step. Vogue says Lykke uses Suntegrity mineral sunscreen with a bit of foundation, and keeps the rest of the routine very pared back.

Use a full sunscreen amount, not a whisper of tinted moisturizer. The makeup part can be minimal; the SPF part cannot.

am.title: Tinted Balm
am.product: RMS Beauty Tinted Daily Lip Balm
am.description: Finish with a low-key tint. Vogue says Lykke loves RMS Beauty lip balm with a natural tint, and Coveteur also says she had started using RMS balms because they are natural, coconut-based products.

pm.title: Makeup Removal
pm.description:
Use first only when there is heavy makeup from a show or event. Vogue says that at night she does the same routine, but removes heavy makeup with coconut oil first.

Massage gently and remove thoroughly so the oil does not sit on the skin as leftover stage makeup glue.

pm.title: Cream
pm.description:
Use as a richer comfort cream when the skin needs a simple, nourishing layer. Coveteur says Lykke keeps a Dr. Hauschka face cream for stage; the exact cream is not named, so this links the brand's classic Rose Day Cream as a plausible face-cream match.

Her Vogue routine later centers Luzern Force De Vie instead, so this is the older backstage option rather than the main current display product.

pm.title: Face Oil
pm.product: NOW Solutions Rose Hip Seed Oil
pm.description:
Use a few drops on face or body when skin feels dry. Vogue says Lykke adds rose hip to her face-oil recipe and rubs that on her body once a day.

Keep it light on the face if coconut oil or richer creams already make the routine feel heavy.

pm.title: Bath + Scrub
pm.description:
Use as an occasional body-scrub ritual, not an every-night face step. Vogue says Lykke missed Korean spa scrubs during pregnancy, so she used Korean scrub gloves at home and drew baths with Epsom salts and lavender oil.

Keep the scrubbing on the body and stop before skin feels raw; melancholy-pop-star bathing should still respect the barrier.

point_description: A practical pregnancy routine for dryness, breakouts, and melasma built around azelaic acid, barrier support, and tinted mineral SPF.

am.title: Gentle Cleanse
am.description:
Massage a small amount over damp skin and rinse with lukewarm water. It is fragrance-free, soap-free, and intentionally simple, which is useful when pregnancy makes previously easygoing skin feel dry or reactive.

If your face is comfortable in the morning, a water rinse is enough. Save the full cleanse for night instead of washing away oil your skin is suddenly struggling to keep.

am.title: Barrier Moisturizer
am.description:
Apply to slightly damp skin. Squalane, glycerin, hyaluronic acid, and ceramides cover dehydration and barrier support without fragrance or essential oils.

Use a lighter layer through an acne-prone T-zone and a more generous one over dry cheeks. Pregnancy skin does not always behave like one uniform skin type.

am.title: Eye-Area SPF
am.product: Cetaphil Sheer Mineral Sunscreen Stick SPF 50
am.description:
Glide the stick onto a clean fingertip, then tap a generous, even layer around the orbital bone and upper eye contour before face SPF. Its mineral sunscreen actives, fragrance-free formula, and drugstore price make it the better fit for this pregnancy routine; the label specifically includes use around the eyes.

This is an eye-area sunscreen rather than a treatment eye cream; the CeraVe eye cream at night handles hydration. Keep it out of the eyes and off the lash line, reapply outdoors, and add sunglasses.

am.title: Tinted Mineral SPF
am.product: Neutrogena Purescreen+ Mineral UV Tint Face Liquid SPF 30
am.description:
Shake well, then apply generously to the face, ears, and neck as the final morning step. The zinc oxide and titanium dioxide provide mineral broad-spectrum protection, while iron oxides in the tint add visible-light protection that is especially helpful when melasma is the concern.

Choose the closest flexible shade and reapply when outdoors. If you prefer an untinted formula, try Vanicream Facial Moisturizer Mineral SPF 30; it may leave more cast, so do not compensate by using less.

pm.title: Gentle Cleanse
pm.description: Cleanse gently for about 30 to 60 seconds and rinse well. If the mineral sunscreen or makeup remains, repeat with the same cleanser rather than adding a fragranced oil or scrub.

pm.title: Azelaic Acid
pm.description:
Smooth a pea-size amount over dry skin two or three nights a week, then work toward nightly use if comfortable. Azelaic acid is the multitasker here: it can help inflammatory breakouts, post-blemish marks, redness, and uneven pigment without using a retinoid or hydroquinone.

A little tingling can happen, but persistent burning is a stop sign. Applying moisturizer first can buffer the treatment if pregnancy has made your skin more sensitive.

pm.title: Barrier Eye Cream
pm.description:
Smooth a rice-grain amount around each eye before face moisturizer. Ceramides, hyaluronic acid, and niacinamide provide fragrance-free hydration without retinoids, bakuchiol, exfoliating acids, or a separate pigment active.

Pregnancy can make familiar skin unpredictable, so patch test and check new products with your obstetric clinician when you have individual restrictions.

pm.title: Barrier Moisturizer
pm.description: Finish with a comfortable layer. On very dry nights, press a small amount of plain petrolatum over flaky areas after moisturizer; it will not treat acne or pigment, but it can make a hormonally temperamental barrier much easier to live with.

point_description: A polished, barrier-conscious routine pairing niacinamide and azelaic acid with a wearable mineral sunscreen for acne, dryness, redness, and melasma.

am.title: Hydrating Cleanse
am.description:
Massage a small amount over wet skin and rinse. The high-glycerin formula cleans without the tight finish that can make pregnancy-related dryness worse, and it can also be used on the body if you want fewer bottles in the shower.

Dry skin can simply rinse in the morning and keep this for the evening.

am.title: Niacinamide Serum
am.product: Kiehl's Ultra Pure High-Potency 5% Niacinamide Serum
am.description:
Apply two or three drops before moisturizer. Five percent niacinamide is a measured supporting active for excess oil, visible redness, uneven tone, and barrier function without turning the routine into a stack of strong treatments.

Begin every other morning. If it makes you flush or itch, skip it; the azelaic acid and sunscreen are the higher-priority concern steps.

am.title: Barrier Cream
am.product: Tower 28 SOS Daily Barrier Recovery Cream
am.description:
Smooth on a light layer while skin is slightly damp. Ceramide NP, allantoin, glycerin, and hyaluronic acid support dry, sensitized skin in a fragrance-free cream that still feels reasonable under sunscreen.

Combination skin can use it only on dry areas in the morning and apply it all over at night.

am.title: SPF Eye Cream
am.product: Supergoop Bright-Eyed 100% Mineral Eye Cream SPF 40
am.description:
Tap an even layer around the eye contour before face sunscreen. The zinc-oxide SPF 40 formula is a reasonable pregnancy option under current mainstream guidance and can help keep facial sunscreen from becoming the stingy part of the morning.

The light peach tint can brighten darkness but will not match everyone. If it does not suit you—or your clinician has given different instructions—bring the approved mineral face SPF carefully around the orbital bone instead.

Read my full glowing review on this product here.

am.title: Tinted Mineral SPF
am.product: Drunk Elephant Umbra Mineral Cream SPF 30/PA+++
am.description:
Apply a full sunscreen amount as the last step and reapply when outdoors. The formula uses zinc oxide and comes in sheer skin-compatible shades; the tint's iron oxides are a useful extra layer of visible-light protection for melasma.

If none of the shades works for you, the untinted Vanicream Facial Moisturizer Mineral SPF 30 is a simpler mineral alternative, with the usual white-cast tradeoff.

pm.title: Micellar Makeup Removal
pm.description:
Saturate a soft cotton pad, hold it over eye makeup or stubborn sunscreen for a few seconds, then wipe gently without scrubbing. This unfragranced sensitive-skin classic removes makeup from the face and eyes while keeping the first cleanse light.

Use it only when you wore makeup, tinted mineral sunscreen, or several layers of SPF; it is not a mandatory nightly tax. Follow with the Gleanser so residue and loosened sunscreen are fully rinsed away.

pm.title: Hydrating Cleanse
pm.description: Massage a small amount over wet skin after micellar water, then rinse thoroughly and pat dry. On bare-skin nights, skip the micellar step and use this cleanser alone; a double cleanse is useful when there is something substantial to remove, not a nightly moral obligation.

pm.title: Azelaic Acid
pm.product: The INKEY List 10% Azelaic Acid Serum
pm.description:
Apply a thin layer to dry skin two or three nights a week, gradually increasing if your skin stays calm. Ten percent azelaic acid addresses blemishes, redness, post-acne marks, and uneven pigment in one step.

Do not chase faster results by applying more. If it stings, use it after moisturizer or reduce frequency; if acne is painful, cystic, or scarring, ask your obstetric clinician or dermatologist about prescription options.

pm.title: Peptide Eye Cream
pm.product: Biossance Squalane + Marine Algae Eye Cream
pm.description:
Press a rice-grain amount around each eye before face cream. Squalane, panthenol, hyaluronic acid, algae-derived antioxidants, and a peptide give dryness and fine lines a cushioned treatment without retinoids, bakuchiol, exfoliating acids, or fragrance.

Confirm personal pregnancy restrictions with your obstetric clinician, especially if eczema or eye-area sensitivity is new.

pm.title: Barrier Cream
pm.product: Tower 28 SOS Daily Barrier Recovery Cream
pm.description: Finish with a generous layer, especially around the mouth and cheeks if they are dry. On nights when your skin feels hot, tight, or unusually reactive, skip azelaic acid and make this the only leave-on step.

point_description: A high-touch pregnancy routine with antioxidant protection, layered hydration, prescription-strength azelaic acid, and premium tinted mineral SPF.

am.title: Gentle Cleanse
am.description:
Dispense into damp hands, work into a light foam, and massage over the face before rinsing. Glycerin, panthenol, aloe, and urea make this the cushioned cleansing step; it is fragrance-free and not meant to leave skin squeaky.

If morning cleansing worsens dryness, rinse with water and use this only at night.

am.title: Vitamin C Antioxidant
am.description:
Press four or five drops over clean, dry skin in the morning. The 15% L-ascorbic acid, vitamin E, and ferulic acid support antioxidant defense and help with dullness and uneven tone, while sunscreen remains the essential melasma step.

Start every other morning if pregnancy has made your skin reactive. Oxidized vitamin C will not earn extra credit, so keep the bottle closed, away from heat and light, and replace it if it turns very dark brown.

am.title: Hydrating Serum
am.description:
Apply a few drops to slightly damp skin after vitamin C has settled. This is the luxury hydration layer for tightness and dehydration; it is optional on humid days or whenever the cream alone is enough.

Hyaluronic acid works best when you seal it in with moisturizer rather than leaving it as the final step on dry skin.

am.title: Rich Moisturizer
am.product: Dr. Barbara Sturm Face Cream Rich
am.description:
Smooth a small amount over the face and neck. Glycerin, urea, panthenol, shea butter, and emollient oils make this the dry-skin anchor; use less through areas that are breaking out.

If it feels too rich beneath sunscreen, reserve it for night and let the hydrating serum plus SPF carry the morning.

am.title: SPF Eye Cream
am.product: Colorescience Total Eye 3-in-1 Renewal Therapy SPF 35
am.description:
Tap an even layer around the lower and upper eye contour before face SPF. This luxury mineral SPF 35 eye treatment adds hydration and color correction, and its tint comes in multiple shades rather than a single peach tone.

If you prefer untinted eye protection—or your obstetric clinician gives different instructions—bring the approved untinted mineral face SPF carefully around the orbital bone and add sunglasses.

am.title: Tinted Mineral SPF
am.description:
Shake well and apply two finger-lengths to the face and neck 15 minutes before exposure, then reapply at least every two hours outdoors. This is a 100% mineral, zinc-oxide SPF with a versatile tint; the iron oxides make it the stronger pick for melasma than an otherwise comparable untinted sunscreen.

If you dislike tint, choose the all-mineral ISDIN Eryfotona Actinica SPF 50+. The untinted finish gives up the tint's extra visible-light help, so a brimmed hat matters even more.

pm.title: Gentle Cleanse
pm.description: Massage over damp skin and rinse thoroughly. If you wore makeup or reapplied water-resistant sunscreen several times, cleanse twice with the same product or use a plain, fragrance-free first cleanser.

pm.title: Prescription Azelaic Acid
pm.description:
Ask your obstetric clinician or dermatologist whether prescription azelaic acid 15% is appropriate, then use it exactly as prescribed. This higher-strength option is the focused treatment for pregnancy breakouts, redness, and uneven pigment; the luxury here is a clinician-guided plan, not a more ornate bottle.

It can sting or dry the skin at first. Do not combine it with improvised peels or extra acne treatments, and contact your prescriber if irritation does not settle.

pm.title: Soothing Eye Cream
pm.description:
Pat a rice-grain amount around each eye before face cream. The fragrance-free formula uses purslane, panthenol, glycerin, macadamia oil, and other emollients for hydration and the look of puffiness rather than retinoids or exfoliating acids.

The brand identifies its Molecular Cosmetics collection as suitable during pregnancy, but your obstetric clinician's guidance still wins when individual sensitivities or restrictions apply.

pm.title: Rich Moisturizer
pm.product: Dr. Barbara Sturm Face Cream Rich
pm.description:
Finish with a comfortable layer to offset dryness from treatment. If azelaic acid is irritating, apply this first as a buffer or take a recovery night with moisturizer only.

Pregnancy-safe is not the same as personally irritation-proof. New or changing pigment, severe acne, eczema, or persistent burning deserves a clinician rather than a more complicated routine.

point_description: A light, acne-conscious K-beauty routine with panthenol, soothing gel-cream hydration, hydrocolloid patches, and the Korean-market sunscreen worth seeking out.

am.title: Gentle Foam Cleanse
am.description:
Use one or two pumps over damp skin and rinse with lukewarm water. The ready-made foam is quick, low-friction, and mild enough for a routine that is more interested in keeping the barrier calm than producing a squeaky-clean feeling.

This is readily available from Ulta in the U.S.; European shoppers can use the same Korean formula through established EU importers. If your skin wakes up dry, skip cleanser and rinse.

am.title: Oil-Balancing Serum
am.product: numbuzin No.1 Pantothenic B5 Active Soothing Serum
am.description:
Apply two or three drops before moisturizer. Panthenol, niacinamide, zinc PCA, and several humectants make this a useful bridge between oily breakouts and dehydration—the combination that makes people over-cleanse and then wonder why everything feels worse.

It is sold directly in the U.S. and through Olive Young Global for many European destinations. The long botanical formula includes alpha-arbutin, licorice, and willow bark, so patch test and avoid it during pregnancy.

am.title: Soothing Gel-Cream
am.product: Dr.G R.E.D Blemish Clear Soothing Cream
am.description:
Smooth on a thin layer, using a little more where skin feels tight. This fragrance-free gel-cream uses glycerin, panthenol, beta-glucan, centella components, and niacinamide to calm visible redness without sitting like a heavy occlusive over acne-prone skin.

The global page links authorized U.S. purchasing; in Korea, look for the Olive Young special sets or 1+1 packs. The Korean product is not inherently better here—the set price and larger promotional bundles are the trip advantage.

am.title: SPF Eye Cream
am.product: Supergoop Bright-Eyed 100% Mineral Eye Cream SPF 40
am.description:
Tap an even layer around the eye contour before the Korean face sunscreen. Korea excels at elegant face SPF, but dedicated eye creams with their own tested SPF remain rare, so this mineral U.S. formula fills a real category gap.

It has a light peach tint. European shoppers who want an untinted option can choose Ultrasun Eye Protection SPF 30; neither is a special Seoul purchase.

Read my full glowing review on this product here.

am.title: Korean SPF
am.product: Beauty of Joseon Relief Sun Aqua-Fresh: Rice + B5 SPF 50+ PA++++
am.description:
Apply generously as the last morning step and reapply when outdoors. This is the lighter Relief Sun: rice seed water and panthenol give it a hydrating, non-greasy finish that suits oily or combination skin particularly well.

U.S. shoppers who want an officially domestic formula can choose Beauty of Joseon Daily Relief Sunscreen SPF 40. In the EU, the SPF 50+ Korean-style formula is sold through the brand's European site. On a Korea trip, I would pick up the Aqua-Fresh SPF 50+ PA++++ Olive Young version or multipack: its newer filter system, higher labeled protection, and weightless texture make it the superior buy versus the separate U.S. SPF 40 formula.

pm.title: Optional Cleansing Oil
pm.product: Haruharu Wonder Black Rice Moisture Cleansing Oil Unscented
pm.description:
Massage one or two pumps over dry skin only when you have makeup or stubborn sunscreen to remove, add water until the oil turns milky, and rinse. The short, fragrance-free oil blend earns its place by doing a job—not because every Korean routine is legally required to double cleanse.

The same formula is available from the U.S. store and Korean-beauty retailers serving Europe. Skip this step on bare-face days or if oil cleansing consistently triggers closed comedones.

pm.title: Gentle Foam Cleanse
pm.description: Follow the oil with one pump over damp skin, or use this as the only cleanse when you did not need the oil. Rinse thoroughly without cleansing brushes or hot water.

pm.title: Oil-Balancing Serum
pm.product: numbuzin No.1 Pantothenic B5 Active Soothing Serum
pm.description: Repeat the serum once daily if evening is the easier time to stay consistent. There is no need to use it morning and night from day one; start once a day and let your skin vote.

pm.title: Snail Peptide Eye Cream
pm.product: COSRX Advanced Snail Peptide Eye Cream
pm.description:
Tap a rice-grain amount around each eye before moisturizer. The light Korean eye cream pairs snail secretion filtrate, niacinamide, and peptides for hydration, brightness, and the look of early fine lines without putting a retinoid into the 20s routine.

It is easy to buy through COSRX in the U.S. and established EU K-beauty retailers. Korea is mainly the place for lower prices and sets; the standard formula is the same.

pm.title: Soothing Gel-Cream
pm.product: Dr.G R.E.D Blemish Clear Soothing Cream
pm.description: Finish with a comfortable layer. If your cheeks are dry but your T-zone is oily, use a full layer on the cheeks and only what you need through the center of the face.

pm.title: Optional Pimple Patch
pm.description:
Place a patch on completely clean, dry skin before serum and cream, choosing one slightly larger than the blemish. The plain hydrocolloid absorbs fluid and keeps fingers away; it is best for a surfaced pimple, not a deep cyst.

The classic version is easy to find in the U.S. and EU. Korea is where to buy the larger multipacks, but the actual patch is not a special superior formula.

point_description: A brightening and early-correction K-beauty routine with rice hydration, ceramide barrier support, gentle retinal, and the Korean Round Lab sunscreen formula.

am.title: Creamy Cleanse
am.description:
Use a small amount over damp skin and rinse. The mildly acidic creamy foam removes overnight oil without creating the tight finish that makes retinal harder to tolerate later.

It is sold through Round Lab's U.S. shop and established EU K-beauty retailers. Unlike sunscreen, this cleanser does not need a special Korean-market hunt; buy the authentic version wherever the price and shipping make sense.

am.title: Milky Rice Toner
am.description:
Shake the two-layer bottle and press a thin layer over clean skin. This is the distinctly K-beauty hydration step: rice extract, emollients, and niacinamide soften the look of dehydration and create a comfortable base for treatment.

It is available through Ulta in the U.S. and iHerb in many U.S. and European markets. Do not keep layering it until your face is sticky just because seven-skin videos exist.

am.title: Brightening Serum
am.product: numbuzin No.5+ Glutathione Vitamin Concentrated Serum
am.description:
Apply a thin layer before moisturizer. Niacinamide, tranexamic acid, vitamin C derivatives, alpha-arbutin, and glutathione make this the concentrated pigment and post-blemish step; sunscreen still does the prevention work.

Start every other morning if you are sensitive. It is now easy to buy through Ulta in the U.S. and Olive Young Global for Europe, so Korea mainly offers better-value double sets rather than a better formula.

am.title: Ceramide Cream
am.description:
Apply a small amount, concentrating it on drier areas. The cream's ceramide, cholesterol, fatty-acid, squalane, and humectant mix is here to make the brightening serum and retinal routine sustainable.

U.S. shoppers can buy it from Sephora; European shoppers can use Olive Young Global. In Korea, the 80 mL cream is often sold in limited bundles or with minis—worth picking up for value, but not because the standard cream is magically stronger.

am.title: SPF Eye Cream
am.product: Supergoop Bright-Eyed 100% Mineral Eye Cream SPF 40
am.description:
Tap an even layer around the eye contour before Round Lab sunscreen. This dedicated mineral SPF 40 eye cream is a U.S. add-on rather than a Korean-market upgrade; Korean face sunscreens are excellent, but the labeled eye-SPF category is still sparse.

The product has a light peach tint. For an untinted European option, use Ultrasun Eye Protection SPF 30.

Read my full glowing review on this product here.

am.title: Korean SPF
am.product: ROUND LAB Birch Juice Moisturizing Sunscreen SPF 50+ PA++++
am.description:
Apply generously as the final morning step. The Korean-market formula uses a modern multi-filter system and wears like a hydrating lotion, making it particularly good for normal, dry, or combination skin.

In the U.S., the official domestic option is the separately formulated Birch Moisturizing UVLock SPF 45+ Broad Spectrum. European shoppers can usually purchase the SPF 50+ PA++++ version through Korean importers. This is a genuine Korea-trip upgrade: seek the tube labeled SPF 50+ PA++++ at Olive Young, because its newer filters, lighter finish, and lower Korean price are preferable to the U.S.-specific UVLock formula. Do not buy from an unverified marketplace seller; the similar packaging makes counterfeits and version confusion too easy.

pm.title: Optional Cleansing Oil
pm.description:
Massage over dry skin to dissolve makeup and water-resistant sunscreen, emulsify with water, and rinse. Use it only when there is something substantial to remove.

Buy through Round Lab's official Amazon storefront or an established K-beauty retailer in Europe. Korea often has cleanser-and-toner sets, but the formula itself is not a reason to carry a heavy oil bottle home.

pm.title: Double Cleanse
pm.description: Follow with a small amount over damp skin, or use it alone when the oil was unnecessary. A calm cleanse is part of the anti-aging routine because irritation is not rejuvenation.

pm.title: Milky Rice Toner
pm.description: Press on one light layer for hydration. On retinal nights, let it absorb fully before the treatment; if even a hydrating toner makes you sting, skip it and keep the routine shorter.

pm.title: Gentle Face Retinal
pm.product: K-SECRET Seoul 1988 Serum: Retinal Liposome 2% + Black Ginseng
pm.description:
Start with a pea-size amount for the face one or two nights a week, keeping it away from the immediate eye area, lip edges, and nose creases. This is a dedicated face serum for early lines, uneven texture, and loss of elasticity. The 2% on the label refers to the encapsulated retinal-liposome complex—not 2% pure retinal—so do not read it as a prescription-strength percentage.

U.S. shoppers can buy it through Olive Young US, while European shoppers can use the authorized retailer LEWKIN Europe. The Korean formula is the same, so an Olive Young Seoul pickup is mainly worthwhile for local pricing or sets rather than extra strength. Do not layer it with exfoliating acids on the same night, and avoid retinoids during pregnancy.

pm.title: Retinal Eye Cream
pm.product: Beauty of Joseon Revive Eye Serum: Ginseng + Retinal
pm.description:
On nights when you are not using the K-SECRET face retinal, tap a rice-grain amount around both eye contours, keeping it out of the eyes and away from the lash line. Here the product is used for its intended eye-area job: ginseng hydration plus gentle retinal for the look of crow's-feet and crepiness.

Start once or twice weekly and do not stack both retinal products until you know the eye area tolerates its own schedule. The same formula is sold in the U.S. and Europe; Korea is worthwhile for lower-priced two-packs, not extra strength.

pm.title: Ceramide Cream
pm.description: Finish with a comfortable layer, or apply it before and after retinal if you need a moisturizer sandwich. On recovery nights, toner and cream are enough; K-beauty layering works best when it stays responsive rather than ceremonial.

point_description: A luxurious mature-skin ritual built around Sulwhasoo ginseng, layered lipid-rich hydration, a carefully introduced Korean retinol, and high-protection Korean SPF.

am.title: Ginseng Cream Cleanse
am.product: Sulwhasoo Concentrated Ginseng Rejuvenating Cleansing Foam
am.description:
Work a very small amount into a creamy lather, massage over damp skin, and rinse. The point of the splurge is a softer cleansing experience for dry mature skin, not permission to wash twice as long.

Sulwhasoo sells this directly in the U.S. and through its international network in Europe. In the morning, water alone is still a perfectly good option when skin feels dry.

am.title: First-Step Serum
am.product: Sulwhasoo First Care Activating Serum VI
am.description:
Press two or three pumps over clean skin before the other serum. This is a Korean-style first serum rather than the final treatment: it adds hydration and slip and makes the richer layers feel more polished.

The U.S. and international versions are readily available. Korea's main advantage is access to generous gift-with-purchase sets and limited packaging; test the fragrant herbal formula before buying the suitcase-sized commitment.

am.title: Ginseng Berry Firming Serum
am.description:
Apply one pump after First Care. The ginseng-berry formula supplies a retinol-free firming and hydration step, so the routine can reserve retinol for the clearly scheduled IOPE treatment at night; it is still a luxury cosmetic, not a substitute for sunscreen or a prescription.

Buy it in the U.S. or Europe when there is a reliable brand promotion. Seoul department stores are better for trying textures and collecting samples, but the standard global formula does not become more effective at passport control.

am.title: Rich Ginseng Cream
am.description:
Warm a pea-size amount between fingertips and press it over the face and neck. The rich emollient texture is the 50s+ choice for lipid loss, tightness, and fine lines made more visible by dehydration.

Choose the classic or rich texture according to your skin, not your age alone. Combination skin may use it only at night and let sunscreen handle daytime moisture.

am.title: SPF Eye Cream
am.product: Colorescience Total Eye 3-in-1 Renewal Therapy SPF 35
am.description:
Apply around the eye contour before HERA sunscreen. This all-mineral luxury eye SPF adds hydration and color correction for darkness, but its tint has to match your skin rather than merely looking elegant on the shelf.

For an untinted European option, use Ultrasun Eye Protection SPF 30. Korea does not currently offer a clearly superior dedicated eye-SPF formula, so this is not a suitcase priority.

am.title: Korean SPF
am.product: HERA UV Protector Multi-Defense Fresh SPF 50+ PA++++
am.description:
Apply generously as the final morning step, including ears and neck. The Korean-market Fresh formula uses a modern multi-filter system in a thin, hydrating finish and is a more realistic partner for several rich skincare layers than a heavy sunscreen cream.

For a straightforward U.S. option, use Sulwhasoo's U.S. UV collection; European shoppers can find the international HERA SPF 50+ PA++++ formula through authorized regional sellers. The Seoul pickup is worthwhile because the current Korean Fresh formula pairs high PA++++ protection and newer filters with an especially light base. It is fragranced, so very reactive skin should test before committing.

pm.title: Optional Cleansing Oil
pm.description:
Massage over dry skin when makeup or water-resistant SPF needs dissolving, emulsify thoroughly, and rinse. Skip it when one gentle cleanse removes everything; ritual is lovely, residue is not.

The same core product is sold in the U.S. and internationally. Korea's gift sets can make it a better-value purchase, but this is not a market-specific formula upgrade.

pm.title: Ginseng Cream Cleanse
pm.product: Sulwhasoo Concentrated Ginseng Rejuvenating Cleansing Foam
pm.description: Follow with a small amount over damp skin and rinse, or use it alone if the oil was unnecessary. If two cleanses leave the face tight, that is useful feedback, not evidence that you need a third hydrating toner.

pm.title: First-Step Serum
pm.product: Sulwhasoo First Care Activating Serum VI
pm.description: Press on a light layer after cleansing. On retinol nights, keep this thin and let it absorb before treatment; skip it if fragrance becomes irritating.

pm.title: Korea-Only Retinol Option
pm.description:
Experienced retinoid users can start with a rice-grain amount for targeted areas one night a week, increasing very slowly. This 0.1% pure-retinol treatment is a genuine Korean-market find from a brand with a long retinol history; it is much more focused than the decorative anti-aging extras in the routine.

For easier U.S. or EU purchasing, use the gentler COSRX The Retinol 0.1 Cream from an authorized regional retailer. Do not combine retinol with exfoliating acids on the same night, and avoid retinoids during pregnancy. More mature skin is not automatically more tolerant, so let comfort—not impatience—set the schedule.

pm.title: Ginseng Berry Firming Serum
pm.description: Press on one pump before cream. This serum does not add another retinoid, but keep the first IOPE nights simple anyway so any irritation has an obvious source; there is no need to debut the entire routine on Monday.

pm.title: Rich Ginseng Cream
pm.description: Finish with a comfortable layer, using it before and after retinol if you need a moisturizer sandwich. On recovery nights, cleanser and cream are completely sufficient.

pm.title: Optional Green Tea Eye Cream
pm.product: AP Beauty Time Response Eye Reserve Cream
pm.description:
Tap a rice-grain amount around the orbital bone when the eye area feels dry. This retinol-free green-tea, shea-butter, niacinamide, and caffeine formula is a comfort and temporary smoothing step, not a requirement for everyone over 50; the face cream can go around the eyes if it does not sting.

It is sold directly in the U.S., while European availability varies. Department-store counters in Seoul are useful for sampling the fragranced texture and comparing local sets before making such an expensive optional purchase.

point_description: A Renée Rouleau-led acne-and-glow routine with deep cleansing, elderberry toner, vitamin C, daily SPF, occasional peel/mask treatments, cold depuffing, microcurrent, and luxury night cream.
